“You can take the scrubs and slippers first.
New slippers are available.
If you will use it often, you can put your name on it.” Nurse Liu waved her hand to chase Cai Qiong away.
Although Cai Qiong was not young, he did not have any impact with his position as a senior attending physician from another hospital.
Cai Qiong also knew it, so he stood aside in a show of alertness.
He then quietly looked at the time while counting how long it took for the chief physician and associate chief physician to shower.
And he waited for a very long time...
In the operating theater, the X-ray films and CT scan films were placed at the other end of the operating table according to Ling Ran’s habit.
Associate Chief Physician Deng and Chief Physician Li entered the operating theater side by side, then they saw those scans, which were simultaneously familiar and unfamiliar to them.
“Did you take these scans?” Associate Chief Physician Deng immediately walked over and stared at the scans.
He felt a sense of familiarity when he looked at the CT scans, but the next second, he doubtfully asked, “Did Cangping District Hospital deploy a CT scan machine to the branch?”
“It’s a portable CT scan machine.
Yunli Medical Company provided it for trial use, so it’s considered a part of the emergency rescue,” Yu Yuan answered with a smile.
When she stood on a stepping stool, she could convey her emotions through her expressions pretty well.
The chief physician and associate chief physician duo had long baths earlier, and their heads were clear now.
Associate Chief Physician Deng found himself stuttering, “Port-Portable CT scan machine?
So generous?”
“Yes, it’s the latest version of 32-slice NeuroLogica’s BodyTom®.
It has its own medical record writing system, although it’s not so useful.
Oh yea, there’s also standard lead shielding...” Yu Yuan was quite fond of advanced medical equipment, so she sounded quite arrogant.
Associate Chief Physician Deng obediently nodded.
A CT scan machine itself was an expensive piece of equipment that cost around ten million, and there was not even a need to mention just how much portable CT scan machines cost.
At the very least, they cost tens of millions.
If they wanted to sign for a long-term service agreement, Associate Chief Physician Deng would not feel strange if that contract cost more than one hundred million.
Meanwhile, in the hospital environment, if such a huge sales deal had to be made, an unknown number of people would definitely be involved to compete for it.
As he looked at the CT scan films in front of him, Associate Chief Physician Deng felt like he saw many doctors like Cai Qiong being abandoned outside the hospital like the lackeys they were...
How could Associate Chief Physician Deng not feel admiration for such a luxurious CT scanner and surgery?
“With the assistance of this portable CT scan machine, you’ve pretty much gained extra strength, Doctor Ling,” Associate Chief Physician Deng chuckled and said something nice.
Chief Physician Li seriously nodded.
“This is the first portable CT scan machine in Changxi Province, right?
Where is the machine?
I haven’t taken a look at it yet.
Oh, how was it sent over?
Was it conveyed by a helicopter?
It should be quite heavy, right?”
“As long as you work hard, you can achieve anything.” Associate Chief Physician Deng chuckled again.
He dared not think about the transportation cost for such an expensive thing.
Ling Ran was performing the surgery, and he did not join the discussion.
It was still Yu Yuan who answered while performing high-level retraction, “This BodyTom® belongs to Yunli Medical Company, we just borrowed from them.
It needs to be returned after we finish using it.”
“Then, Yunli Medical Company will sell it like a new one?
That’s not very good, right?”
“This BodyTom® is a financial asset of Yunli Medical Company.
It’s a product of financing leasing.” Mai Chun stood at a corner, and she spoke weakly.
Yunli Medical Company’s business has grown so much,” Associate Chief Physician Deng said, and he was struck with awe.
As someone working in the hospital, he knew how hard it was for a pharmaceutical sales company to conduct business, and he also knew how high the cost was to make a financing leasing.
If many medical companies that specialized in medical equipment could grow very fast and smoothly after their startup, then the financial leasing for medical equipment business would be even riskier.
Associate Chief Physician Deng even felt his teeth aching at the thought of the cost when he thought about it.
Let’s watch the surgery.” Chief Physician Li also felt the same, but he had long since made himself aloof to worldly matters, so he felt slightly better.
Associate Chief Physician Deng shrugged.
When he wanted to say something, his phone rang.
“Excuse me.” Associate Chief Physician Deng walked to a corner to pick up the call.
After a moment, Associate Chief Physician Deng put down his phone, went back to the operating table, looked at Ling Ran, and asked, “Doctor Ling, you know Wei Jiayou, right?”
“Who?” Ling Ran frowned, but it was because he was stripping the patient’s portal vein.
“Wei Jiayou.
He specializes in cardiovascular surgeries.

He’s Academician Di’s student, and he also likes abdominoscopy...” Associate Chief Physician Deng described him and said, “He said that’s coming to support the Bazhaixiang hospital branch on behalf of Academician Di.”
“Oh,” Ling Ran answered.
Yu Yuan introduced Wei Jiayou again from the side.
“He’s the ginseng baby, the one who likes to wear the ginseng scent.”
“Oh...” Ling Ran said with a drawl this time and nodded.

chapters.title: Chapter 870 Confident and Calm
paragraphs: When Wei Jiayou got off from the helicopter, his hands were in his pockets while he let the wind caused by the helicopter fan blade to blow up his clean white coat. He did not even blink.
“Is there no one responsible for reception?” Wei Jiayou walked from the newly built helipad in the backyard to the backdoor of the small building by himself.
“I’m following you.” Yu Yuan’s voice was low, and her eyes stared straight ahead.

“Oh, Doctor Yu.” Wei Jiayou could not remember people, but his impression toward Ling Ran and Yu Yuan were strong enough. He smiled lightly and said in a superior tone, “Doctor Yu, you don’t even look at people when you talk now, huh?”
“I’m smelling you.” Yu Yuan sounded calm yet alert.
Wei Jiayou was stunned, but he showed a smile on his face. “Eau de Gentiane Blanche is still very aromatic, right?”
Yu Yuan secretly thought that ginseng without the smell of chicken was definitely a little bit tasteless.
However, Yu Yuan did not counter his words since he had just arrived. She just pouted and continued to lead the way.
From the limited conversation they had earlier, Yu Yuan’s impression toward Wei Jiayou was very bad.

This guy was not only arrogant, but he also wanted to compete for the authorship of an article last time when Ling Ran’s treatment group met Wei Jiayou. Although they held different opinions, it was still a competition.

For one, Academician Di, whom Wei Jiayou followed, was always an aggressive kind of person. Last time, they organized a show of force and intimidated many local hospitals. Now, Wei Jiayou was said to have come to support them, but the exact situation remained uncertain.
Besides, Wei Jiayou’s fame had already started growing, so when he came to Changxi Province again, he did not need Academician Di to come along with him. He himself was already an intimidating force.
The only thing that could be said about what Academician Di did was that it gave off a very outstanding impact, despite the fact that he gave a bad impression to the doctors in the local hospitals.
Naturally, they did not bother about the impression they gave to the doctors in local hospitals.
For doctors like Academician Di, the doctors in local hospitals only needed to be obedient at specific moments.

Wei Jiayou also possessed a similar attitude. He followed Yu Yuan for a while as if he was following the arrow signs on roads. After they walked for a while, he asked, “Are you still able to spare some people to form a treatment group? Is there any doctor who is willing to join me voluntarily?”
His words made him seem very egotistical, but that was also because he was a very egotistical person, because Wei Jiayou received this kind of treatment in most hospitals.
For him, this was the standard.
Yu Yuan understood why Zuo Cidian asked her to welcome Wei Jiayou now. If he sent Lu Wenbin over, this ginseng baby might end up being sent to the Emergency Department at the last of his breath.
“We’ll be quite busy for now, so we can’t allocate anyone for you for the time being,” Yu Yuan said tactfully.
Wei Jiayou lowered his head and looked at her, then he said, “With my participation, your team won’t be so busy. This is what we call support.”
Yu Yuan smiled and thought secretly. ‘We are busy serving Doctor Ling. Can you provide support for this?’
Wei Jiayou saw her unwillingness, so he said from another perspective, “What surgery are you guys doing? Still hepatectomy?”
“Still?” Yu Yuan came to a screeching halt.
Wei Jiayou could not help but raise his head slightly. He felt that Yu Yuan’s figure had slowly become larger and taller. Her shoulders rose, her upper body became longer, and her heels even rose.
“I’ve also performed some hepatectomies recently, so if it’s hepatectomy, I think I’m able to help out.” Wei Jiayou walked along the side and took the opportunity to bypass Yu Yuan.
“We did some hepatectomies. Doctor Wei, you’re a cardiologist, right?” Yu Yuan’s strides were smaller, but she walked fast. She followed Wei Jiayou closely like a leopard chasing after an antelope.
Wei Jiayou could not help but feel slightly flustered. “I don’t only do cardiovascular surgeries, I also perform abdominoscopy.”
“So, now, your surgical scope is overlapping with Doctor Ling’s?” Yu Yuan calmly, quietly, and peacefully stared at Wei Jiayou.
“Overlapping...” Surgeons having their surgical scope overlapping with each other is something normal, right? Besides, we are not doctors from the same hospital.”
Yu Yuan stared at Wei Jiayou with bright eyes. “You’re right.”

Wei Jiayou looked away, but he realized what he did on the next second, so he immediately became firm with his attitude again. He stretched out his neck and looked down on Yu Yuan. “That’s the truth. There’s not only one doctor who performs hepatectomy, right?”
“But there are not many who can perform it well.” When Yu Yuan talked about it, she softened her tone and asked, “Do you want to perform a hepatectomy?”
“It’d be great if there is any.” Wei Jiayou smiled faintly and said, “Give me an operating theater and a team of people. I’ll reduce half of the workload for you. I think it should be alright.”
When Wei Jiayou said that, he regained his confidence, which was the overconfident state that the people described.
He did indeed have reason to be confident.

People said one could know everything once he mastered one skill. Wei Jiayou was able to master cardiovascular surgeries at a young age. While that was because he had the guidance of a great teacher, his own qualities also served as the precondition for him to be able to master cardiovascular surgery at his age.
On the other hand, hepatectomy was considered the top of the crop for general surgeries, but when compared with the meticulousness and risks in cardiovascular surgery, it was inferior.

Naturally, it was not easy to perform any surgery meticulously and control the risks. Even tonsillectomy had the possibility of leading to pulmonary embolism, which meant that there was not even a need to mention how much riskier it was for major surgeries.

Wei Jiayou had seen Ling Ran’s surgery before, so he recognized Ling Ran’s ability in hepatectomy. However, that was in a well-equipped operating theater, and it was an elective surgery while the patient received complete preoperative preparations.
The disaster in Bazhaixiang would not provide such a good condition to Ling Ran.

He needed to adapt to the situation, needed to use his own experience and team management skills, readapt to an unfamiliar environment, unfamiliar equipment, as well as unfamiliar medical conditions and complications...
That was what Wei Jiayou was good at.
Recently, Wei Jiayou received training given to a fire captain.
“Let’s take a look at your operating theater first. Oh yeah, I can grab this chance to greet Doctor Ling.” Wei Jiayou’s smile was very clearly the smile of a victor.
Yu Yuan caught a glimpse of Wei Jiayou, but she could not figure out his thoughts at the moment, so she only led the way at the front with her head bent.
Wei Jiayou watched as Yu Yuan slowly blended into one with the arrow signs on the road; his mind was calm and peaceful.
Before he came, he had searched for information on Bazhaixiang, and he designed a plan and added a back-up plan. Now, he only needed to act according to the situation.
Wei Jiayou was delighted because of his thoughts, and he walked faster.
“Be careful, don’t bump into it.” A medical staff stood at the corner of the stairs and blocked Wei Jiayou.
“What...?” Before Wei Jiayou finished his words, his eyes caught sight of the automatic, round machine in front of him. He could not help but murmur, “Is this BodyTom?”
“Yes, it’s a new portable CT scan machine,” Yu Yuan explained.
“Do you know how expensive this thing is?” Wei Jiayou tried to prove himself.
Yu Yuan slowly nodded. ” Yes, I know. It costs a few warehouses. ”

Wei Jiayou did not understand why the unit of measurement for the price was that of a warehouse, but he still nodded sternly. His emotions surgery while he sized up the portable CT scan machine as it moved past him.

chapters.title: Chapter 871 Exposed
paragraphs: “Excuse me.” Lu Wenbin pushed the portable CT scan machine. He carefully put forth the strength in his arms.

The new BodyTom was not hard to push. If it were on the flat floor of Yun Hua Hospital, one person could easily move it. To be on the safe side, two people would move it, with one pushing and the other pulling. They would also have to control their speed.

Bazhaixiang, naturally, could not be compared to tertiary Grade A hospitals in terms of infrastructure. The portable CT scan machine was basically used as a fixed CT scan machine, but it would be moved every day to make it easy for critical patients, and 30% of its function could be said to have been brought into play.
Wei Jiayou observed every detail of the BodyTom with a scrutinizing gaze.
BodyTom was one of the most high-end CT scan machine models, and Wei Jiayou started using them in Beijing a few years ago. At that time, it was even reported by a newspaper.

However, even until now, portable CT scan machines were not common goods. At least half of the provinces among thirty provinces in the country did not even have one, whereas most of the doctors in the country had not even seen this machine before.

However, Wei Jiayou believed that he could distinguish a real and fake BodyTom based on his familiarity with the machine. Wei Jiayou did not know whether there was a fake portable CT scan machine, but he felt it was extremely normal if Bazhaixiang used a fake one. At the very least, it was a second-hand item made to look like a new product.
Wei Jiayou kept observing and staring at it until he heard someone snickering beside him.
Wei Jiayou turned around to look, and he saw a middle-aged doctor smirking at him.

When he saw Wei Jiayou turn around, that middle-aged doctor did not feel embarrassed. Instead, his smile faded away. He looked at Wei Jiayou with empathy and said, “It’s your first time seeing one, right? It’s a portable CT scan machine, so it’s an advanced technology, and it’s ridiculously expensive. It’s quite fun.”
“I’ve seen it before.” Wei Jiayou gritted his teeth.

“You’ve seen it? That’s normal, too. I’ve even seen the throne, mind you. Oh well, why am I saying that to you? Sigh, let me tell you something else. Young men like you all might have seen the world, but when you’re now in a small town and in a lower rank hospital to boot, just do whatever you should, and don’t bite off more than you can chew. Alright, I’ll just stop here. Consider myself to have been too chatty and offended another person. Ah... I just wasted my time talking.”

This middle-aged doctor was Cai Qiong. One of his ways to relieve his depression was to tease other young doctors in the ward area, scold resident doctors, and educate housemen and interns. These could make him feel happier and persist for one more day.

Cai Qiong used this way to insist on not resigning, but the only consequence was that after ten to twenty years, the young doctors he teased previously had become attending physicians and even held the position of associate chief physicians, and this made his living environment outside the General Surgery Department more difficult...
However, Cai Qiong should retire in another twenty years.

Therefore, when he saw a good-looking doctor daydreaming, Cai Qiong took the opportunity to give his “advice”. He left right after he finished talking to prevent the doctor from defending himself and affecting his mood.
For Cai Qiong, such handsome doctors really affected people’s emotions sometimes.
“He seems quite familiar.” Cai Qiong frowned slightly when he was far away.
Wei Jiayou was basically fuming, especially when he lowered his head and saw Yu Yuan covering her mouth while giggling. Wei Jiayou felt so angry that he was shivering.
But his pride did not allow him to fly off in a rage.
Yu Yuan continued leading the way in front, and her movements became lighter.

“Go in. After showering, you can look for Doctor Ling in the operating theater.” Yu Yuan asked for scrubs, keys, and other items from Nurse Liu, who was in charge of guarding the place today. Then, she passed them to Wei Jiayou and gave him another piece of advice, “We are now performing surgeries back to back. Doctor Ling has a high requirement toward aseptic operations, so pay more attention to that. Don’t let the circulating nurse catch and chase you out, or else, it’ll be very awkward for you.”
“I got it,” Wei Jiayou answered in a muffled voice.

Yu Yuan saw him enter in the manner of someone who was not very bright in the head, and she could not help but sigh. “What I’m saying is that you shouldn’t wear perfume. If they recognize you and know that you’re a doctor from another hospital, the nurse will not be polite.”

Yun Hua Hospital was also the top hospital in the region. Throughout the year, hundreds to thousands of doctors came for in-service training, and there were even more people who went to observe Ling Ran’s operations. Ling Ran had high requirements as well, hence, the nurses who were familiar with Ling Ran and often set things up for him were really strict when they needed to be strict.
Wei Jiayou pursed his lips and lowered his voice. “Eau de Gentiane Blanche is very mild, and it does not affect the surgery...”
“You can make the decisions all you want if you’re the chief surgeon. If you’re not, don’t put the blame on others when you get scolded. ” Yu Yuan acted like she had already warned him.
Wei Jiayou stood at the door, hesitated for a few seconds, and said, “Even if I don’t wear the perfume, there will still be some scent lingering.”
“What?”
“I’ve worn it for quite a long time, so maybe I’m stained with its scent. It’s impossible to wash it away after a bath,” Wei Jiayou explained helplessly.
Yu Yuan almost burst into uncontrollable laughter. “So, you’re pickled!”
Wei Jiayou’s expression became stiff, and he quickly rushed into the shower room.
In the operating theater, Ling Ran started the second surgery in the afternoon.

Once plenty of equipment, as well as new instruments, were sent into the operating theater and after they changed the rules for continuous surgery, Ling Ran alternated between using two operating theaters, and his surgical volume every day was 50% of the surgeries performed in Yun Hua Hospital.

Naturally, he included minor surgeries like debridement in the Emergency Department. The advantage in it was that his assistants could rest more. There were only two operating theaters anyway, and the doctors who were not on duty could all wake up naturally in the morning before they went for an unprotected sleep. There was absolutely no issue whatsoever in them waking up when the sky was bright, after all.
Ling Ran himself would perform the surgery as meticulously as possible.
The Perfect Surgery mission was not really a mission to him, but more like a reminder.
Ling Ran himself chased after perfection, but the high number of patients and surgeries unintentionally generated a large amount of stress on him, and it caused Ling Ran to be indecisive.

Right now, now that he was in a Bazhaixiang that still suffered through geographical limitations but the patients’ need for surgery was not high, Ling Ran could naturally complete the Perfect Surgery mission.
From Ling Ran’s perspective, performing perfect surgery did not mean completing every surgical step accordingly but taking more flexible measures that were more suitable for the patient.
In the operating theater, Ling Ran decided to first pay close attention to the exposure of the liver surgery.

Usually, when he did a surgery, Ling Ran used the bilateral subcostal incision the most, which meant that he would perform a V-shaped incision on the patient’s tummy, then open up the abdomen above the belly button.

The exposure in that method was good, and it pretty much provided a very high coefficient of safety when used in highly difficult surgery like a hepatectomy. However, if he wanted to become even better, that kind of incision would basically destroy all the muscles in the upper abdomen. The patient would have a hard time recovering, and it also easily caused psychological expectation for a surgery, which would deal heavy damage to the body. It was not considered the perfect choice.
It was especially so when he faced a tumor at the border of the liver or had to perform hepatectomy on a smaller part of the liver. In truth, he could absolutely use a small incision for the surgery.
As Ling Ran thought in this way, he stared at the patient’s CT scan and made a small incision at the right costal margin.
“Huh? You’re making such a small incision?” Ma Yanlin the assistant was stunned.
“Yes, for the surgery today, this incision is enough.” Ling Ran’s tone was confident and firm.
The young nurses in the operating theater heard the voice and looked at Ling Ran. Then, they squealed in their hearts.

Oh well, why am I saying that to you?
Sigh, let me tell you something else.
Young men like you all might have seen the world, but when you’re now in a small town and in a lower rank hospital to boot, just do whatever you should, and don’t bite off more than you can chew.
Alright, I’ll just stop here.
Consider myself to have been too chatty and offended another person.
Ah...
I just wasted my time talking.”
This middle-aged doctor was Cai Qiong.
One of his ways to relieve his depression was to tease other young doctors in the ward area, scold resident doctors, and educate housemen and interns.
These could make him feel happier and persist for one more day.

Cai Qiong used this way to insist on not resigning, but the only consequence was that after ten to twenty years, the young doctors he teased previously had become attending physicians and even held the position of associate chief physicians, and this made his living environment outside the General Surgery Department more difficult...
However, Cai Qiong should retire in another twenty years.
Therefore, when he saw a good-looking doctor daydreaming, Cai Qiong took the opportunity to give his “advice”.
He left right after he finished talking to prevent the doctor from defending himself and affecting his mood.
For Cai Qiong, such handsome doctors really affected people’s emotions sometimes.
“He seems quite familiar.” Cai Qiong frowned slightly when he was far away.
Wei Jiayou was basically fuming, especially when he lowered his head and saw Yu Yuan covering her mouth while giggling.
Wei Jiayou felt so angry that he was shivering.
But his pride did not allow him to fly off in a rage.
Yu Yuan continued leading the way in front, and her movements became lighter.
“Go in.
After showering, you can look for Doctor Ling in the operating theater.” Yu Yuan asked for scrubs, keys, and other items from Nurse Liu, who was in charge of guarding the place today.
Then, she passed them to Wei Jiayou and gave him another piece of advice, “We are now performing surgeries back to back.
Doctor Ling has a high requirement toward aseptic operations, so pay more attention to that.
Don’t let the circulating nurse catch and chase you out, or else, it’ll be very awkward for you.”
“I got it,” Wei Jiayou answered in a muffled voice.
Yu Yuan saw him enter in the manner of someone who was not very bright in the head, and she could not help but sigh.
“What I’m saying is that you shouldn’t wear perfume.
If they recognize you and know that you’re a doctor from another hospital, the nurse will not be polite.”
Yun Hua Hospital was also the top hospital in the region.
Throughout the year, hundreds to thousands of doctors came for in-service training, and there were even more people who went to observe Ling Ran’s operations.
Ling Ran had high requirements as well, hence, the nurses who were familiar with Ling Ran and often set things up for him were really strict when they needed to be strict.
Wei Jiayou pursed his lips and lowered his voice.
“Eau de Gentiane Blanche is very mild, and it does not affect the surgery...”
“You can make the decisions all you want if you’re the chief surgeon.
If you’re not, don’t put the blame on others when you get scolded. ” Yu Yuan acted like she had already warned him.
Wei Jiayou stood at the door, hesitated for a few seconds, and said, “Even if I don’t wear the perfume, there will still be some scent lingering.”
“What?”
“I’ve worn it for quite a long time, so maybe I’m stained with its scent.
It’s impossible to wash it away after a bath,” Wei Jiayou explained helplessly.
Yu Yuan almost burst into uncontrollable laughter.
“So, you’re pickled!”
Wei Jiayou’s expression became stiff, and he quickly rushed into the shower room.
In the operating theater, Ling Ran started the second surgery in the afternoon.

Once plenty of equipment, as well as new instruments, were sent into the operating theater and after they changed the rules for continuous surgery, Ling Ran alternated between using two operating theaters, and his surgical volume every day was 50% of the surgeries performed in Yun Hua Hospital.
Naturally, he included minor surgeries like debridement in the Emergency Department.
The advantage in it was that his assistants could rest more.
There were only two operating theaters anyway, and the doctors who were not on duty could all wake up naturally in the morning before they went for an unprotected sleep.
There was absolutely no issue whatsoever in them waking up when the sky was bright, after all.
Ling Ran himself would perform the surgery as meticulously as possible.
The Perfect Surgery mission was not really a mission to him, but more like a reminder.
Ling Ran himself chased after perfection, but the high number of patients and surgeries unintentionally generated a large amount of stress on him, and it caused Ling Ran to be indecisive.

Right now, now that he was in a Bazhaixiang that still suffered through geographical limitations but the patients’ need for surgery was not high, Ling Ran could naturally complete the Perfect Surgery mission.
From Ling Ran’s perspective, performing perfect surgery did not mean completing every surgical step accordingly but taking more flexible measures that were more suitable for the patient.
In the operating theater, Ling Ran decided to first pay close attention to the exposure of the liver surgery.

Usually, when he did a surgery, Ling Ran used the bilateral subcostal incision the most, which meant that he would perform a V-shaped incision on the patient’s tummy, then open up the abdomen above the belly button.
The exposure in that method was good, and it pretty much provided a very high coefficient of safety when used in highly difficult surgery like a hepatectomy.
However, if he wanted to become even better, that kind of incision would basically destroy all the muscles in the upper abdomen.
The patient would have a hard time recovering, and it also easily caused psychological expectation for a surgery, which would deal heavy damage to the body.
It was not considered the perfect choice.
It was especially so when he faced a tumor at the border of the liver or had to perform hepatectomy on a smaller part of the liver.
In truth, he could absolutely use a small incision for the surgery.
As Ling Ran thought in this way, he stared at the patient’s CT scan and made a small incision at the right costal margin.
“Huh?
You’re making such a small incision?” Ma Yanlin the assistant was stunned.
“Yes, for the surgery today, this incision is enough.” Ling Ran’s tone was confident and firm.
The young nurses in the operating theater heard the voice and looked at Ling Ran.
Then, they squealed in their hearts.

chapters.title: Chapter 872: Non-Standard
paragraphs: The moment Wei Jiayou walked through the door, the first thing that entered his sight was the tall and handsome Ling Ran.
Even though he had already expected him to be there, he could feel every single one of his brain cells become more energized the moment he saw Ling Ran.
Wei Jiayou had to muster all of his pride to turn away and look at the patient on the operating table.

The patient was in a supine position, and a few doctors were crowding around him. There was basically no way for Wei Jiayou to see what was going on inside the patient’s open abdominal cavity. However, Wei Jiayou was certain that a hepatectomy was being carried out just by looking at the compression pants and thermal pants that the patient was wearing. Aside from that, he had also learned about the situation beforehand.

“Shh.” Yu Yuan had entered the operating theater before Su Jiafu, and right then, she was standing on a stool and watching the surgery. Su Jiafu was standing beside her, and he seemed to be upset because he did not get to sit down.

Even though she was standing with her back facing the door, she could tell from the footsteps and the accompanying aroma that Wei Jiayou, the man who wore ginseng-flavored perfume, was the one who entered the operating theater.

Wei Jiayou had obviously noticed this too. He furrowed his eyebrows in resignation. ‘Does this dwarf have the sense of smell of a dog? I have showered three times with L’Occitane body shampoo before I came over.’
Yu Yuan pointed at Ling Ran and placed her index finger on her lips to gesture at Wei Jiayou to keep quiet. She then pointed at the patient before she turned away and continued watching the surgery.
Undaunted, Wei Jiayou pursed his lips. But he did not utter another sound.

If he were in another hospital or in an operating theater where another doctor was carrying out the surgery, he would not have been so obedient. He had been following his teacher to hospitals all over the country for a show of force, and it was never his intention to appear adorable. He had provoked countless people before.

However, most of the time, he only dared to provoke another person when he was sure that that person was inferior to him. And Wei Jiayou definitely did not feel this way about Ling Ran. Even until now, he could still remember the way Ling Ran carried out prolonged CPR.
As a cardiothoracic surgeon, Wei Jiayou had performed CPR countless times. But Ling Ran’s maneuvers were deeply ingrained in his mind.

Every compression Ling Ran made was on point. More importantly, Ling Ran was able to persist and carry out CPR on a patient for more than one hour, with the confidence to bring him back to life. And most importantly, Ling Ran brought the patient back to life for real, and the patient did not suffer from any sequelae up until the time he got discharged...

At the end of the day, as a doctor, results spoke louder than words. There was no point in talking about mere theories. There were plenty of researchers who were PhD graduates for that, and when it came to their specializations, they could totally thrash clinicians in a debate. But when it came to practical applications of those theories on a single patient, researchers were far inferior to clinicians.

Even until now, Wei Jiayou had not been able to replicate Ling Ran’s feat when it came to prolonged CPR. Of course, this could be attributed to the fact that he was always busy and did not have many opportunities to perform CPR. However, he was unable to perform the kind of prolonged CPR Ling Ran was capable of, and that was the cold hard truth, which always bothered Wei Jiayou.

And to make himself feel better, he planned to defeat Ling Ran when it came to hepatectomy, which was what Ling Ran was best at. At least, he wanted to defeat Ling Ran in the Bazhaixiang hospital branch.
Wei Jiayou looked around the unfamiliar operating theater. He quickly memorized the placement of everything and recalled the usage of equipment of various models...

As he looked around, Wei Jiayou realized that the equipment and facilities in this operating theater looked very similar to the equipment and facilities that he had seen before in another operating theater...

“You guys are also participating in the rescue efforts here? Isn’t the Bazhaixiang hospital branch under the jurisdiction of Cangping District Hospital? Yun Hua Hospital is really generous. This anesthesia monitor is a Phillips model, isn’t it? Wow, even equipment used in rescue efforts nowadays are imported.” Wei Jiayou was truly familiar with all kinds of equipment, and it only took one glance for him to tell whether a piece of equipment was locally-manufactured or imported. Moreover, he was also pretty well-versed when it came to the relationship between various smaller hospitals and larger hospitals. In this respect, he was unlike other doctors his age, who only cared about operating on patients...
Yu Yuan tip-toed a little to get a better view of the surgical field. She said in a soft voice, “This operating theater is a reconstruction.”
“What do you mean by reconstruction?” Wei Jiayou was a little confused.

“Basically, we duplicated Yun Hua Hospital’s operating theaters in the Bazhaixiang hospital branch. For that purpose, we brought in some equipment and facilities of higher quality. This is what it means.”

“A complete duplication?” Wei Jiayou was astonished. Even though the facilities in an operating theater ranged from very cheap to very expensive, duplicating an operating theater definitely cost a lot more than renovating a house.
Plus, from what he could see, duplicating the operating theater definitely cost a lot more than renovating a house.

Yu Yuan knew that Wei Jiayou was astonished, and she was secretly pleased. She continued, “We didn’t purchase these equipment and facilities. We borrowed them from a medical company. After the situation over here gets better, we’ll either ship them back to Yun Hua Hospital or pay rent to the medical company.”

Ever since the Emergency Department of Yun Hua Hospital was upgraded into Yun Hua Emergency Medical Center, they pumped in money for expansion every month. It was very possible for them to either build a new operating theater or replace the equipment in one of the operating theaters.
Wei Jiayou smacked his lips and looked at Ling Ran. He could not help but feel a little envious.

He never had the privilege to be treated that way. Forget about duplicating an operating theater. Right now, he did not even dare to ask for a personal operating theater. Academician Di was the one who called the shots in his department, after all, and he was merely Academician Di’s favorite student.

Truth be told, Academician Di might not even get to enjoy the privilege of such a treatment. Even though hospitals made a lot of money, because of the initial construction of basic infrastructure, most hospitals nowadays owed banks a lot of money. No hospital would dare to spend so much money on such a thing.

“We do enjoy a lot of freedom in local hospitals,” Wei Jiayou said those emotional words in a conceited manner. He then took a few steps forward to stand beside Yu Yuan and looked at the operating table.
The most eye-catching part of the operating table was the patient’s liver, which was exposed courtesy of the abdominal retractor. A group of medical staff members was surrounding it.

The stainless steel abdominal retractor was silver, and it sparkled under the light. There was not a single drop of blood on it. It held the patient’s abdominal muscles and adipose tissue apart, and it could not be helped that some pale-yellow adipocytes were exposed.

The patient was slightly plump. If he were clothed, his body proportions might still look fine. But after an incision was made with an endotherm knife on his skin, a yellow layer of adipocytes could be seen. It was closely adhered to the skin, and its thickness was more than one inch. Some semicircular adipose granules could even be seen, and they looked like the pearls inside cups of bubble tea. Half of them were buried amid the adipocytes.

Wei Jiayou glanced at the adipose layer, and then at the liver. His attention was then captured by the small incision Ling Ran had made. He arched his eyebrow a little and muttered, “It’s a non-standard incision? Who’s the patient?”
“He’s a local. He came over for a physical examination since it was free, but the scans hinted at early-stage liver cancer,” Yu Yuan answered without turning to look at Wei Jiayou.
“Is he a local official or something?”
Yu Yuan furrowed her eyebrows, a little triggered. “What’s with the question?”
“Aren’t non-standard incisions only made when the patient is someone of status?” Wei Jiayou sounded confident.
As he had been practicing hepatectomy, he had met many people from the General Surgery Department and the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery.

Nowadays, during hepatectomy, surgeons basically only made bilateral subcostal incisions. Every now and then, for right lobe hepatectomy, they would make reverse L-shaped incisions. Non-standard incisions were very rare.

On one hand, it was because open abdominal surgery was a well-developed field. A bilateral subcostal incision was basically enough for most ordinary cases of hepatectomy. There were very few cases that could not be performed using bilateral subcostal incision and reverse L-shaped incisions.

On the other hand, making a non-standard incision made hepatectomy even more difficult. Even for excellent doctors, unless their patient was someone of power and influence who could afford special care, they would usually make a standard incision. No one would make life difficult for themselves for no reason.
Yu Yuan kind of understood what Wei Jiayou meant. She arched an eyebrow and replied in a serious tone, “The patient is a local farmer. He doesn’t have any relative who’s an official either.”
“Then, why has a non-standard incision been made?”
“Doctor Ling feels that this kind of incision is more suitable for the patient’s condition,” Yu Yuan replied.
Wei Jiayou had cocked his eyebrows originally, now, he could not help but let them fall.

chapters.title: Chapter 873: Small Incision
paragraphs: “So, Doctor Ling thinks that such an incision is suitable. But what’s your opinion?” Wei Jiayou watched as the surgery progressed, and he suddenly muttered a question.
Yu Yuan, who was standing on her toes, suddenly realized how tiring the position was. She stopped tiptoeing and pointed at herself in surprise. “Are you asking me?”
“Of course.” Wei Jiayou looked around, and even though Associate Chief Physician Deng was flashing him an obsequious smile, he merely nodded.

Even a smile was enough to make Associate Chief Physician Deng from the General Surgery Department of Yun Hua Provincial Hospital extremely happy. Associate Chief Physician Deng was a student of Academician Di’s unofficial student, who in turn ended up in Changxi Province. In Wuxia terms, Associate Chief Physician Deng would be an outer sect member, while Wei Jiayou would be a last disciple. There was a huge difference between their statuses.

Hence, because of this relationship between them, Wei Jiayou could give Associate Chief Physician Deng a call and order him to make arrangements and come here. However, there was no need for Wei Jiayou to do anything in the interest of Associate Chief Physician Deng or even treat him in a friendly manner.
Right now, Wei Jiayou was paying Yu Yuan more attention compared to Associate Chief Physician Deng.

Yu Yuan had always been interested in theoretical discussions. When she heard Wei Jiayou’s question, she tilted her head and started pondering. She looked like a lopsided Shiitake mushroom. “I feel that if a doctor is skillful enough, a small incision would of course be more suitable.”
“Ah... you are still young.” Wei Jiayou could not help but reply Yu Yuan with what Academician Di often said about himself.
“What do you mean?” Yu Yuan puffed her cheeks, and she looked like a Shiitake mushroom that had been soaked in water.

“A small incision makes the surgery more difficult. You mentioned that a small incision should be made if the doctor is skillful enough. But how would the doctor know if he is skillful enough without opening the patient’s abdominal cavity? Even though hepatectomy isn’t as dangerous as cardiothoracic surgeries, it’s not a walk in the park...”
“If everyone follows your line of thought, no one would be making small incisions anymore. Everyone would make nothing but big incisions.”

“That’s why I said that you’re still young. Only young doctors like to make small incisions, as this serves as proof to their skills. As for experienced doctors, they care more about preventing errors.” Wei Jiayou paused for a moment as he pondered. He then added, “You know, if you make a bigger incision at the beginning of the surgery, no one would think that you’re a lousy surgeon. But if you only realize that the incision you have made is too small in the middle of the surgery, and have no choice but to make it bigger, everyone would know that you have made a wrong judgment earlier...”
Yu Yuan was speechless. She blinked as she looked at Wei Jiayou and said, “I’ve never thought that a ginseng baby could have such complicated thoughts. You’re actually a dang shen , aren’t you?”

There were many things that Wei Jiayou wanted to say, but he was unable to utter any of them. In the end, he shook his head in resignation. “In conclusion, everyone usually makes a standard incision for safety purposes. Hepatectomy is a risky surgery, and anything might happen. If an accident were to happen after you make such a non-standard small incision, you will have no way of defending yourself if the patient ends up suing you.”
Yu Yuan looked like she was deep in thought as she nodded.
Wei Jiayou could not help but flash a smile. “What I said makes sense, don’t you think so?”

“At the end of the day, you just aren’t confident when it comes to hepatectomy, right?” Yu Yuan looked at Wei Jiayou with a meaningful gaze. Thirty percent of it was the kind of look one has when he saw through another person, thirty percent of it was understanding, and forty percent of it was pity.
When Wei Jiayou heard that, he was extremely heartbroken. He said with determination, “I never lack confidence at surgery.”
“Even your grammar is wrong.” Yu Yuan pursed her lips in disdain. She looked like an examiner.
“It’s time to remove the left and right coronary ligaments,” Ling Ran reminded. He paused for a moment to let the words sink in. He then continued with the surgery.
Wei Jiayou sucked in a sharp breath when he heard that. He whispered, “It’s quite difficult to remove the coronary ligament with such a small incision.”
Yu Yuan was clumsy, but she was very well-versed when it came to medical theory. Right now, her expression was solemn too.

A coronal plane is any vertical plane that divides the body into ventral and dorsal sections. The coronary ligaments were located on the coronal plane of the liver, and they were basically parallel to the peritoneum. In other words, when a doctor operated on a patient who was in a supine position, they would not be able to get a full view of the coronary ligaments.
If the doctor had made a standard large incision, there would be many workarounds to this. However, Ling Ran had made a small incision today.
Yu Yuan could not help but feel a little worried as she looked at Ling Ran.
However, at this moment, there was a scrutinizing expression on Ling Ran’s face.
Yu Yuan took another good look at Ling Ran. She was right. Ling Ran was... finding this interesting.
Indeed, Ling Ran found this interesting.

He had made some speculations regarding the condition of the patient’s coronary ligaments when he read the patients scans. But he was only able to know the exact condition after opening the patient’s abdominal cavity.
This was also the hardest part of this surgery.
Ling Ran liked to be challenged.

It was not just about the small incision. Even smaller incisions were also possible for hepatectomy. However, the operating theater in Bazhaixiang was not that well-equipped. Aside from this, hepatectomy with a small incision, after all, required more intuition on the surgeon’s part, and it also had certain unique surgical features which were suited for it.
To Ling Ran, this kind of challenge was hard to come by.
In a way, it was also the kind of surgery that Ling Ran desired to perform but rarely had the chance to.
Whenever a challenge arose in the middle of such a surgery, Ling Ran would feel like he was served a surprise dish during a scrumptious meal.
He was not in a hurry either as he worked his way down in a leisurely manner.
He used the retractor when he should, separated tissues when he should, and obstructed blood flow when he should...
If a person was not looking at the rest of the operating table and merely focusing on Ling Ran’s hand, they would probably think that Ling Ran was a good cook who was making a delicious dish.

After they took their focus away from Ling Ran’s hands and looked at the rest of the operating table, they would notice the reality of the difficulty Ling Ran was facing in operating the patient, and this would give them a totally different realization.
“The patient’s coronary ligaments have been removed,” Ling Ran reminded his assistants again. He then examined the surgical field for a moment and said, “I’ll resume blood flow for now.”
As he spoke, Ling Ran removed a pair of forceps that was used to obstruct blood flow.
Wei Jiayou arched an eyebrow, and he put even more focus on the surgery.
“Bazhaixiang is quite a suitable place to carry out hepatectomy with a small incision, isn’t it?” Yu Yuan felt rest assured when she saw this, and she turned to look at the ginseng baby.
Wei Jiayou refused to show any signs of weakness. He insisted, “Erm... but it’s not as applicable as laparoscopy. Aside from this, it’s also safer to carry out hepatectomy with a large incision...”
“This means that making a small incision is the most suitable choice,” Yu Yuan said and snorted. “Beside, there’s something that you didn’t realize.”
“What?” Wei Jiayou immediately started racking his brain. He was wondering what he had missed.
Yu Yuan smiled and said, “Hepatectomy is cheaper when the incision made is smaller.”
Wei Jiayou was speechless. “Does this small sum of money make any difference?”

“I don’t know how things are in other places, but many of the people in Bazhaixiang aren’t well off.” Yu Yuan paused for a moment and continued, “Of course, the most important thing is making sure that the patients get well and live a little longer.”
“Of course...” Wei Jiayou’s voice drifted off as he replied.
Of course he wanted to make sure that the patient got well and save the patient’s life. But as it seemed, he would not be able to put his hepatectomy skills to use today.
“Surgical thread.” Ling Ran’s voice rang out again, snapping Wei Jiayou out of his reverie.
“Suturing a small incision... This isn’t an easy feat.” Wei Jiayou tried to emulate the maneuvers involved in stitching up a small incision with his bare hands as he watched the surgery.

But what’s your opinion?” Wei Jiayou watched as the surgery progressed, and he suddenly muttered a question.
Yu Yuan, who was standing on her toes, suddenly realized how tiring the position was.
She stopped tiptoeing and pointed at herself in surprise.
“Are you asking me?”
“Of course.” Wei Jiayou looked around, and even though Associate Chief Physician Deng was flashing him an obsequious smile, he merely nodded.
Even a smile was enough to make Associate Chief Physician Deng from the General Surgery Department of Yun Hua Provincial Hospital extremely happy.
Associate Chief Physician Deng was a student of Academician Di’s unofficial student, who in turn ended up in Changxi Province.
In Wuxia terms, Associate Chief Physician Deng would be an outer sect member, while Wei Jiayou would be a last disciple.
There was a huge difference between their statuses.
Hence, because of this relationship between them, Wei Jiayou could give Associate Chief Physician Deng a call and order him to make arrangements and come here.
However, there was no need for Wei Jiayou to do anything in the interest of Associate Chief Physician Deng or even treat him in a friendly manner.
Right now, Wei Jiayou was paying Yu Yuan more attention compared to Associate Chief Physician Deng.
Yu Yuan had always been interested in theoretical discussions.
When she heard Wei Jiayou’s question, she tilted her head and started pondering.
She looked like a lopsided Shiitake mushroom.
“I feel that if a doctor is skillful enough, a small incision would of course be more suitable.”
“Ah... you are still young.” Wei Jiayou could not help but reply Yu Yuan with what Academician Di often said about himself.
“What do you mean?” Yu Yuan puffed her cheeks, and she looked like a Shiitake mushroom that had been soaked in water.
“A small incision makes the surgery more difficult.
You mentioned that a small incision should be made if the doctor is skillful enough.
But how would the doctor know if he is skillful enough without opening the patient’s abdominal cavity?
Even though hepatectomy isn’t as dangerous as cardiothoracic surgeries, it’s not a walk in the park...”
“If everyone follows your line of thought, no one would be making small incisions anymore.
Everyone would make nothing but big incisions.”
“That’s why I said that you’re still young.
Only young doctors like to make small incisions, as this serves as proof to their skills.
As for experienced doctors, they care more about preventing errors.” Wei Jiayou paused for a moment as he pondered.
He then added, “You know, if you make a bigger incision at the beginning of the surgery, no one would think that you’re a lousy surgeon.

But if you only realize that the incision you have made is too small in the middle of the surgery, and have no choice but to make it bigger, everyone would know that you have made a wrong judgment earlier...”
Yu Yuan was speechless.

You’re actually a dang shen , aren’t you?”
There were many things that Wei Jiayou wanted to say, but he was unable to utter any of them.
In the end, he shook his head in resignation.

Hepatectomy is a risky surgery, and anything might happen.
If an accident were to happen after you make such a non-standard small incision, you will have no way of defending yourself if the patient ends up suing you.”

Thirty percent of it was the kind of look one has when he saw through another person, thirty percent of it was understanding, and forty percent of it was pity.
When Wei Jiayou heard that, he was extremely heartbroken.
He said with determination, “I never lack confidence at surgery.”

She looked like an examiner.

He then continued with the surgery.

Right now, her expression was solemn too.

In other words, when a doctor operated on a patient who was in a supine position, they would not be able to get a full view of the coronary ligaments.
If the doctor had made a standard large incision, there would be many workarounds to this.

However, at this moment, there was a scrutinizing expression on Ling Ran’s face.
Yu Yuan took another good look at Ling Ran.
She was right.

chapters.title: Chapter 874: Why?
paragraphs: “He used titanium clips on the bile canaliculus, sutured the main bile ducts directly, and then used the endotherm knife to stop the bleeding, huh? Doctor Ling’s bleeding control is quite good.”
“Looking at it now, the exposure of the operating field is pretty clear.
“Yeap... the incisional edge is clear.”
When Wei Jiayou got serious, his understanding of Ling Ran’s operation immediately rose by one level, and his expression also changed slightly.

Yu Yuan listened to him muttering to himself, and she could not help but glance at Wei Jiayou before looking at his hand movements, quickly growing entranced. Then, she observed carefully for a few seconds, and surprisingly, she felt a slight pang of envy.

When it came to mastering surgical information, having followed Ling Ran in hundreds of operations, her theoretical foundation was solid. It could be said that she had some understanding of everything no matter how big or trivial it was.
However, when she moved down the skill tree of the medical field and arrived at the bottom, which was practical application, Yu Yuan always felt herself falling short.

This was like how a non-athlete commentator or an amateur athlete did sports reviews. There would always be a difference in levels between them and professional athlete commentators. This will be especially prominent when they commented about the players’ actions on the field and how filthy their locker rooms were. At the end of the day, they could only obtain information about those things through rumors and gain a general idea of what went on.

For example, someone like Wei Jiayou had never performed a hepatectomy with a small incision, but he had performed all sorts of incisions when performing cardiovascular surgery. His technical skills were taught and guided by experts, and he had experience in performing liver surgery himself. The feeling he gained would not only be different, his grasp in minute details would also be completely different.

In comparison, Yu Yuan only had the role of an assistant in hepatectomy. There were plenty of times where she may only be the second or third assistant. It could be said that she never once had the opportunity to hold a living liver in person.

If she had never held a liver before, she would not be able to experience the touch of the liver in her hands, and she would not have the opportunity to cut the liver to experience how tender it was, and she would not know what the important parts were while flipping a liver over in her hands...
When Yu Yuan saw Wei Youjia’s hand movements coming to a pause, she then whispered, “Are you stealing ideas?”

“I’m just here to steal... take a glance at the operation, why would you say so?” Wei Jiayou’s hands subconsciously clenched into a fist, as if he was trying to prevent someone from seeing his finger movements.
Yu Yuan smiled, but did not speak again.
Wei Jiayou forcefully turned his head and looked at the surgery again. Then, he suddenly felt that watching the surgery was meaningless.

If he could not secretly ste... If he could not learn and learn effectively, what was the use of just watching Ling Ran performing surgery? Even if Ling Ran was handsome, he could not just watch him for a few hours.

“Doctor Ling, which do you think has the most promising development between hepatectomy with small incisions and laparoscopic hepatectomy?” Wei Jiayou broke the silence of the operating theater and ignored the gazes from the other young doctors.
Ling Ran raised his head, stretched his neck, and looked at Wei Jiayou. Then, he said, “For future development, laparoscopic hepatectomy should be more promising.”

“Isn’t it so?” Wei Jiayou did not expect Ling Ran to answer so decisively. After using an auxiliary phrase, he smiled and said, “Well, since you’re now performing a hepatectomy with a small incision, wouldn’t you be easily eliminated?”
Ling Ran thought for a while and said, “Hepatectomy with a small incision is indeed easier to nitpick.”
The young doctors and nurses in the operating theater looked at Wei Jiayou with a hostile look. This provocative act was not welcomed in any situation or place.
Wei Jiayou was willing to bear that hostility. As he was doing his show of force around the country, he had received too many various attacks, and these hostile gazes were nothing.

“Doctor Ling, you shouldn’t perform hepatectomy with small incisions just because you are young and the technique is not yet perfected. There may be some advantages in performing hepatectomy with a small incision now, but wait for another ten to twenty years, and at that time, perhaps even laparoscopy would be obsolete. It is estimated that surgical robots such as the da Vinci Surgical System would have become common. At that time, even if you can perform hepatectomy with a small incision well, what use is there to it? The patient won’t want to go through with it.” Wei Jiayou seemed to be speaking from Ling Ran’s point of view, and he sounded quite tactful.
“But the patient still needs it now.” Ling Ran turned his head around and cast Wei Jiayou a look. “And it’s just by coincidence that I have a suitable technique.
“A suitable technique?” Wei Jiayou did not really understand what he meant.

“For this patient, a hepatectomy with a small incision would be the right technique.” Ling Ran lowered his head again. While performing the operation, he said, “No matter what happens in the next ten or twenty years, that would not affect the current value of a hepatectomy with a small incision. ”

“But if you spend the same amount of time you spend refining your skills with hepatectomy performed through small incisions in refining your skills with laparoscopes, you can also help many people, and there’s greater development prospects for it.” Wei Jiayou gave some input of his own ideas.
Ling Ran nodded, but said, “I agree, but small incisions would be suitable for today’s surgery. When I return to Yun Hua Hospital, I may use laparoscopes a little more.”
“Hmm? Do you know how to perform a laparoscopic hepatectomy?” Wei Jiayou furrowed his brows.
“Of course.” Ling Ran’s tone made it sound as if it was only obvious that he knew.
Wei Jiayou frowned deeply. “You just started with it, right? I searched your papers, none of them talked about laparoscopic liver resection ...”
Yu Yuan interjected. “Doctor Ling doesn’t have the habit of writing two papers about one operation.”
Wei Jiayou heard her mocking tone, but still focused on Ling Ran. “Since you know how to do laparoscopic hepatectomies, why do you still perform one with a small incision?”

“Isn’t it making its use known over here right now?” Ling Ran gave a modest smile. After all, it was a technique given by the system. Although many people in his life gave him many gifts, the gifts given to him by the system were still rather hard to explain.

Wei Jiayou naturally found it more difficult to understand. “What’s the use of it making its use known here? Do you know how many times you would actually be able to use it? You can use the same amount of time and energy you spend learning this on something else, and you can improve those skills even further.”

Ling Ran saw that he was being aggressive, and he worried that it would affect the operation. Hence, he told the truth, “It doesn’t take much time and energy, so it doesn’t matter. Hmm... Nurse Liu, Lu Wenbin, please take Doctor Wei out to rest first.”
As Ling Ran watched Wei Jiayou’s face turn red with rage, he was really worried that he would rush up to the operating table.
Lu Wenbin shook his thirty-eight inch arm and took the lead to stand in front of Wei Jiayou.
Wei Jiayou’s feet did not move at all. Even when he was blocked by Lu Wenbin’s chest, he raised his voice. “I don’t believe it.”
“What do you not believe?” Lu Wenbin sighed. “Do you understand what a genius is?”
Wei Jiayou said proudly and boldly. “I have seen many genii. Genii are everywhere.”
Lu Wenbin looked down at Wei Jiayou, sighed again, turned his head around, gestured with his chin in a direction. “Look at your face and look in the mirror. Aren’t you ashamed of yourself?”
Wei Jiayou calmed down at this time, looked at Ling Ran, and slowly said, “I will apply for an abdominoscope for hepatectomy to be delivered here. We’ll see who’s right when the time comes.”
“Sure.” Ling Ran nodded. “With the relevant equipment, there would be even more choices.”

“Then, it’s settled. In at most a week, no more than ten days, I can get it over here,” Wei Jiayou said extremely boldly. It was naturally extremely difficult to transport an equipment which was worth millions across thousands of miles in one breath within a week or two.
“We will also equip Doctor Ling with a full set of equipment.” Mai Chun, who was hiding in the corner of the operating theater and holding a phone, said timidly.

chapters.title: Chapter 875: Something Does Not Feel Right
paragraphs: Early next day with a barely risen sun, Wei Jiayou freshened up and sprayed some Hermes Eau de Gentiane Blanche before going to the hospital’s cafeteria for breakfast.
As soon as he got a bowl of hot soy milk, Wei Jiayou picked up a piece of deep-fried dough stick. Before he could dip it in, the sound of the helicopter’s propeller came from the air.

“Hospitals these days are so rich. Helicopters could fly here from day to night. Whereas for us, we’ll always be emptying our pockets when we go to the hospital.” The diners next to his table were dissatisfied with the disturbance as they complained about the situation while drinking soy milk.
Wei Jiayou glanced at the other side and ignored them. People who drank soy milk instead of dipping deep-fried dough sticks in it were not worthy of respect.
“Boss, I’ll pay with WeChat.” Wei Jiayou finished eating quickly, wiped his mouth, and went to the hospital after paying for his meal. When he entered, he saw a lively scene.

The hospital will never be lacking patients and their families, but there were a lot more medical staff than what he usually saw, but he did not know whether they were reinforcements or whether all the medical staff in the hospital had gathered together.
Wei Jiayou grabbed a young resident doctor and asked, “What kind of patient was just delivered by helicopter?”
“It’s Yunli Medical Company’s helicopter. I think they’re just sending over an instrument.” The resident doctor’s face was full of obedience, fully hiding his inner anxiety and complaints...
Wei Jiayou said, “They sure are rich. Say, is Yun Hua Hospital ready to settle down here or something? The instruments are delivered in batches.”

“It’s financial leasing, so we’re really just borrowing the equipment. I don’t think it’ll cost a lot of money if we return it after using it, right?” The resident doctor looked innocent and cute, but no one knew whether it was real or whether he pretended to look that way.
Wei Jiayou chuckled. “Are capitalistists all synonymous with philanthropists now?”
But even though he said those words, he still released the resident doctor and ran to the outpatient department.

His application for equipment had been sent through his senior brother. By then, once they sent over some specialized instruments and he borrowed some existing equipment in Bazhaixiang, the equipment and instruments for laparoscopic hepatectomy should be ready.

Among these, what Wei Jiayou wanted the most was a fully automatic high-flow pneumoperitoneum insufflator, a high-definition camera and display system, easy-to-use ultrasound equipment, and adjustable laparoscopic ultrasound probes...
If possible, Wei Jiayou even wanted to get an anesthetist he was familiar with...
However, these were only needed during surgery.
And if he wanted to perform surgery, he must first have a patient!
Without peers introducing patients to him, doctors will have to mainly rely on outpatient consultations and the Emergency Department to get patients.

No matter how great Wei Jiayou was, it would be difficult for him to show his capabilities without patients. When he was in Beijing Hospital, Wei Jiayou did not have to worry about such things. Now that he came out here himself without a powerful person supporting him, he had to make preparations himself.

This was one of the reasons why Academician Di allowed him to come out. He had already gone on a show of force, and Wei Jiayou had already gained his fame. Now, Wei Jiayou had to experience firsthand how to use that fame to get what he wanted.
Part of the reason why Wei Jiayou did not go straight to tertiary Grade A general hospitals was because of consultations.

Patients who went to the tertiary Grade A general hospitals usually had higher requirements, especially in the local tertiary Grade A general hospitals. Since there was not much of a difference in price between a specialist slot and a normal slot, the older specialists were basically the ones who can receive all the patients.
For young people like Wei Jiayou, it was difficult for them to gain trust, and it was even more difficult for him to gain the trust of patients who needed surgery.

In contrast, patients visiting Bazhaixiang hospital branch would not care about the age of the doctors as much. On one hand, Bazhaixiang hospital branch was always a hospital in a village, and those who would come for consultation would not have major illnesses. On the other hand, there were a total of only two full-time doctors in Bazhaixiang hospital branch. If there was anything commendable about them in terms of their medical skill, it would be that these senior doctors could often prescribe cheap and amazing cold medicine, and the expectations of the people toward them were only about that much.
Wei Jiayou found the office assigned to him and turned on the computer with familiar ease.

As an outpatient clinic, this was nothing new to him. If Bazhaixiang hospital branch used the electronic medical record system, he may need to familiarize himself with the system, but if they were just using paper medical records, it would not be much of a hindrance to him.
“It sure came fast.”
“Yunli Medical Company’s so efficient.”
“Is it really because it’s Yunli Medical Company? It’s because Doctor Ling is great.”
Wei Jiayou heard the continuous discussion in the hallway and could not help but frown. He then stood up and walked to the door.
“What were you guys talking about?” Wei Jiayou wanted to sound friendly, but his tone was still haughty.
“We were just talking about the new machine that Yunli Medical Company has just delivered,” a young doctor replied.

“A high-definition camera, high-throughput pneumoperitoneum insufflator, ultrasonic knife or something...” the young doctor whispered.
“A set of hepatectomy equipment.” Wei Jiayou interrupted the young doctor and said slowly.

“Where are the machines placed?” Wei Jiayou hurriedly asked.
“Waiting to be sent into the operating theater, I guess” said the young doctor. ‘I mean, where else could it go?’

He did not want to go too fast so as not to show his impatience.
“Ginseng is here.” As soon as Wei Jiayou entered the surgical corridor, he heard a familiar female voice inside.
Female surgeons were still very rare in a hospital. Wei Jiayou did not even need to spend time thinking, he already conjured up the top of Yu Yuan’s head in his mind.
“Bring my Red String of Fate,” Lu Wenbin shouted purely out of humorous purposes, but opened the door himself.
“I hear that your equipment has arrived.” When Wei Jiayou saw the situation, he decided to be blunt and voice the purpose for his visit.
“It’s being configured.” Lu Wenbin gave way, like a door panel being pushed aside.
Wei Jiayou nodded and stepped in, and he saw a row of seven or eight men in white clothes standing or kneeling around while they were busy with work.
Wei Jiayou could not help but look at Yu Yuan.
“Doctor Ling asked for them to come as soon as possible,” Yu Yuan explained without him asking.
“A helicopter can’t carry so many people, yes?”
“Yeah.” Yu Yuan felt that there was no need to give an answer to that question.
Wei Jiayou exhaled long and heard. “Pharmaceutical sales companies these days are so generous.”

“As long as the doctors can successfully complete the surgery, it’s okay for us to work a little harder.” Tian Qi, also dressed in white, came over, but her aura was so powerful that she could not be ignored.
Wei Jiayou glanced at Tian Qi, and his throat instantly seized up. He originally had his speech prepared, but he could not say it now.
“Is there enough manpower?” Tian Qi asked the engineers who were working hard.
“No problem.”
“We’ll definitely be able to complete our task as scheduled.”
“It’s going smoother than we expected.”
The engineers started talking, and they looked excited.

Now, Yunli Medical Company was reborn. Not only was its stock price surpassing what it was worth during its heyday in the past, it was still increasing aggressively. The engineers did not have many opportunities to meet its legendary director, Tian Qi.
Tian Qi nodded slightly, looked at Wei Jiayou again, and smiled. “Is the request for your equipment going smoothly, Doctor Wei? Do you need help?”
If someone else had said that to him, Wei Jiayou would definitely think they were mocking him. At least, when he spoke like this, he would definitely be mocking someone.
However, when he looked at Tian Qi’s expression, Wei Jiayou only shook his head and gave a smile. “It went well, and it should be delivered as scheduled.”
“That’s good. Doctor Ling’s workload is too much. I hope that Doctor Wei can join in as soon as possible.” Tian Qi greeted everyone before leaving the operating theater with a cheerful smile.
When Wei Jiayou saw her leaving and thought about what she said, he felt that something did not feel right.

chapters.title: Chapter 876: I Have a Plan
paragraphs: “Senior brother, sorry to trouble you this time round.” Wei Jiayou spoke into his phone sincerely.

“Sure, no problem. We can’t be defeated by a local hospital, right? If we are not any better in terms of shifting instruments than the local hospital, it’s a disgrace to all of us.” The voice of his senior brother could be heard clearly from the phone, and he sounded prideful as well.
Wei Jiayou smiled and said politely, “Senior brother, you’re truly very attentive.”
This time, if not for the help from his senior brother, the instrument he requested would only arrive after one to two weeks. By that time, Ling Ran could have performed countless hepatectomies.
According to Wei Jiayou’s observation over the past few days, he was really worried that Ling Ran would clear off all the patients in Baizhangxiang.

Those diseases that required hepatectomy were usually developed over months and years. Rural places like Bazhaixiang had a low floating population, and if Ling Ran truly treated all the patients, it would be useless for Wei Jiayou to get the instruments, as the town had no more sick patients for him, no matter how good he was.
However, Wei Jiayou took legal channels for his instruments to arrive. If his senior had not helped him, it would be very difficult for him to speed up the transportation of instruments to him.
His senior was excited as well. He chuckled and said, “It’s mainly because they’re respecting our master. I heard that you want to use it. Doctor Wei, we’re counting on you for the glory.”
“Of course. Rest assured.” Wei Jiayou replied, and his confidence level was very high.

“However...” His senior brother changed the topic of conversation and reminded him, “While you can dabble in hepatobiliary surgery, your main focus should be on cardiovascular surgery. Cardiovascular surgeries are the real cream of the crop, understand?”
“I understand that,” Wei Jiayou uttered some words to placate his senior brother before he ended the call. His mindset was already focused on the new instruments.

With the complete set of laparoscopy instruments, he can start performing hepatectomy. For a young man like Wei Jiayou, he was not interested in using his power to suppress others, instead, he was more excited to use his skills and talents to show off and suppress others.

Wei Jiayou put down his phone and hummed while showering. After changing into a set of new clothes, he put on Hermes Eau de Gentiane Blanche, and he released the scent of herbs used to treat patients.
The walking ginseng baby walked around Bazhaixiang.
The people’s nickname for him and mocking words about him in private would not affect Wei Jiayou.
He walked around leisurely at Bazhaixiang as though he was roaming around his new territory.
A patient was enveloped in a floral-patterned bed sheet when he passed by Wei Jiayou. A row of liquid hung above his gurney.
Wei Jiayou’s gaze swept through the transfusion bags, and he noticed a few familiar drug names. He immediately stopped and asked the accompanying doctor at the side, “Is he a hepatectomy patient?”

“Yes.” The accompanying doctor was Ren Qi, the surgeon from Qiu Province who went to Yun Hua Hospital for in-service training. His chubby appearance made him look friendly, and while he replied in a most amicable tone.
Wei Jiayou misunderstood and kept asking, “How’s the condition of the patient?”

As a senior attending physician from a county hospital, Ren Qi was familiar with the operation mode of Bazhaixiang branch hospital and was able to adapt to it. He also knew how to handle the outdated instruments in the hospital branch. In fact, he was familiar with it. Without even his knowledge, he grabbed quite a lot of chances to perform surgeries. For young people like Wei Jiayou, Ren Qi would not even give him any chance to seize the surgery from him. However, he still spoke politely, “I’m not the doctor in charge, so I don’t know his situation too well.”
“Okay...” Wei Jiayou could do nothing about it, since Ren Qi did not know what happened. He could not just interrogate him, after all.
“Doctor Wei, if there is nothing else, we’ll enter the operating theater first,” Ren Qi said politely, and the gurney was pushed in.
Wei Jiayou nodded and saw Ren Qi moving forward. He asked, “Can you go to the operating table today?”
This topic of conversation made Ren Qi grin. He smiled and said, “I’m the first assistant for today.”
“Oh,” Wei Jiayou replied and said, “While you are holding the lens, you need to lift it slightly higher...”
Ren Qi changed his expression and listened carefully.
Even though he was wary of Wei Jiayou, he could not dismiss his skill.
At that moment, he would place more attention on Wei Jiayou if it meant that he could pick up something new.
Wei Jiayou casually gave some remarks for a minute before he said, “Why are you the assistant today?”

“Old Lu and the others are exhausted.” Ren Qi smiled sincerely. If they were not exhausted, he would not have the chance to perform surgeries. Ren Qi was thankful for his years of experience in the county hospital. It was precisely because he had stayed for a long time at the county hospital that he sent to the helicopter by Zuo Cidian, who shared similar experiences with him. It was also because there were few doctors who came along that he could quickly have the chance to perform surgery...
“So, Ling Ran performed a lot of surgeries over the past few days?” Wei Jiayou’s words put a stop to Ren Qi’s pride.
Ren Qi felt his heart freeze, and he immediately said, “It’s time. I need to go for surgery.”
As he spoke, Ren Qi immediately entered the Operating Area. He did not know why Wei Jiayou wanted to know with the questions he asked, but he knew that he cannot be the one who leaked the secret.
Wei Jiayou frowned and looked at Ren Qi’s back before he fell into an inexplicable state of gloominess.
What should he do if the livers of the hepatectomy patients were all removed by Ling Ran?

Honestly speaking, for Wei Jiayou, who was always based at Beijing Hospital, he would never have to think of this question. In Beijing, there were too many patients, and regardless of which hospital or doctor working there, they would either die by overworking, die of fatigue, or just die suddenly.
Wei Jiayou had never thought that he would be worrying about this question.
Wei Jiayou frowned and thought about this hard, and he finally got a solution.

“Free treatment? Are you really giving free treatment for everything?” The person in charge of Bazhaixiang Health Department looked at the plan Wei Jiayou brought out and instantly perked up. “The costs the patients will have to bear by themselves once their medical insurance covers their treatment will be paid by you, and they can even claim from you for the medicine they have to buy for themselves?”

“Yes. We have special funding for this.” When Wei Jiayou said this, he was actually a little reluctant. He was using the funding he had for his specific purposes. Although he had quite a lot of funds for specific purposes because of his master, the cost a patient will have to pay for hepatectomy surgery was still quite high.
“Thank you, Doctor Wei. Give my thanks to your hospital as well...” The person in charge thanked Wei Jiayou sincerely, because what he received was something most practical.
Wei Jiayou nodded silently and said, “There is a quota for this. Please explain it to the patients as well.”
“Of course,” the person in charge replied firmly.

Wei Jiayou was relieved when he returned to Bazhaixiang hospital branch. In this case, even if Bazhaixiang did not have much of a floating population, the local patients would still not all be taken by Ling Ran.
Wei Jiayou laid on the reclining chair and sprayed some Eau de Gentiane Blanche into the air before he smiled and let the mist from the perfume envelope him.
At this moment, cheers were heard from the ground floor.
“It’s cleared!”
“It’s cleared!”
Those cheers soon became uniform.
Wei Jiayou slowly got up, opened the window, and looked down.

At this moment, a van slowly drove over. Someone carried a megaphone and shouted, “The road outside Bazhaixiang is repaired. Everyone, please be patient and give priority to the disaster relief personnel and disaster relief resources. We will give priority to patients and the army to pass through first...”
The person with the megaphone repeated his words twice and drove off the street.
Wei Jiayou slowly sat back on the chair, and he suddenly felt as if he just suffered an extremely huge loss to the zenith degree...
