chapters.title: Chapter 877: In High Spirits
paragraphs: Ling Ran exited the operating theater and washed his hands again. He then massaged his own neck and sat languidly in a chair in the rest area.
Chief Physician Li was sitting beside him in an equally lackadaisical manner.

He preferred to be involved in matters related to public health. However, as a chief physician from the General Surgery Department, he could not just sit idly by when there were surgeries that had to be performed. He did not mind operating on all the patients that Ling Ran did not want to operate on, anyway.

The General Surgery Department was the department that covered the most types of surgeries to begin with. In a place like Bazhaixiang, only orthopedic surgeries and general surgeries could be carried out. It was basically impossible to carry out more complicated and specialized surgeries such as surgery for brain trauma here. This was true even if the best neurosurgeon in the world was in Bazhaixiang, as the facilities here were limited. This kind of patient would have to be transferred to Yun Hua, or even Beijing, for a chance at life.
However, Chief Physician Li was not carrying out as many surgeries as Ling Ran, and the main reason that caused his fatigue was his advanced age.
Chief Physician Li sighed internally as he gazed at Ling Ran’s youthful complexion. He then said, “I heard that the repairs are completed, and the roads are usable already.”

“Huh? That’s great.” Ling Ran could not help but perk up. Now that the roads were usable, it would be easier for medical consumables and drugs to be transported to Bazhaixiang hospital branch. Even if a person were to disregard other things, Bazhaixiang hospital branch was almost running out of gauze as it was used in the operating theater every day.
“Do you plan to return to Yun Hua anytime soon?” Chief Physician Li asked probingly.
Ling Ran found this slightly curious. He asked, “Aren’t we on a rescue mission? The fact that the roads are now usable doesn’t mean that it’s time for us to leave, right?”
“Of course,” Chief Physician Li quickly said. He could not help but straighten up and say, “Do you plan to stay here until the rescue mission ends?”

To him, it was a very comfortable thing to have Ling Ran as part of the Bazhaixiang rescue mission. The worst thing that could happen to a person who was involved in public health was unsupportive leaders, society’s lack of understanding, and doctors’ reluctance to get involved, even though it was also reality that the leaders did not support them, society did not understand them, and doctors refused to work.
However, Chief Physician Li wanted to carry on with the project. If Ling Ran left, he would lose a powerful supporter.
Ling Ran never cared about this kind of complicated stuff. He said matter-of-factly. “I plan to operate on another bunch of patients before going back. I’m not in a hurry.”

He was on a Perfect Surgery mission, and up until now, he had only completed around thirty cases of perfect surgeries. In the beginning, he was only capable of achieving perfection in two or three surgeries every day. Even now, the numbers had only gone up to around three or four. It was never more than five. This meant that more than half of the surgeries he performed were not done perfectly. To Ling Ran, this was unacceptable.
This was imperfection!
Because of the circumstances, Ling Ran was not in a hurry to return to Yun Hua.

On one hand, it was because it was not yet time for the medical team from Yun Hua Hospital to leave. Aside from this, there was also a relationship between a surgeon and the operating theater as well as surgical facilities and equipment he was using, where the surgeon would perform well if he was familiar with these things.
The more familiar a surgeon was with an operating theater and all its aspects, the higher the probability of him carrying out a perfect surgery.
This was also the reason why Ling Ran had been able to perform more and more perfect surgeries every day.
Of course, this could also be attributed to the fact that his skills had leveled up. However, this was also correlated to the upgrade of instruments in his environment.

Ling Ran already possessed Master Level Hepatectomy, and it was extremely difficult for him to improve any further. He could only feel like he was going forward whenever he carried out a perfect surgery.
Hence, Ling Ran was naturally not in a rush to return to Yun Hua Hospital.

Chief Physician Li did not know what was on Ling Ran’s mind, but he was so happy that he flashed a bright smile. “That’s great. I plan to stay here for some time as well. We can continue to work together to improve the healthcare in Bazhaixiang.”
Ling Ran did not comment, but he did not mind working together with Chief Physician Li.

Both public health and infection control were extremely boring tasks. If it were not for Chief Physician Li’s presence, Ling Ran might have to spend some time carrying out these tasks. At least, he would need to allocate two or three assistants for this.
Ling Ran found it useful to have a chief physician who was willing to carry out tasks related to public health around. Moreover, Chief Physician Li was quite good at it.

“Since the roads are usable now, the problems with occupational exposure and lab work can be dealt with.” Ling Ran had always had a mind of his own. Since all the stars were aligned for him to carry out surgeries now, he was naturally thinking ahead.

Ling Ran did not care much that Bazhaixiang hospital branch was not where he was mainly based. He did not mind seeing the hospital branch as a subsidiary, either. He only cared about having access to patients and operating theaters, as these were all he needed to show his worth...

Chief Physician Li assumed that this was one of Ling Ran’s demands that was a prerequisite for him to work with Ling Ran. He did not seem surprised as he thought about it. “It’s easy to deal with the problem of lab work. I can find someone from Yun Hua Provincial Hospital. I know a good medical laboratory technician. He’s quite skilled.”

“It would be best if he can train a local to become a medical laboratory technician.” Xiang Xueming had been listening in to the conversation, and he immediately spoke out when he saw that they were talking about something crucial.

Chief Physician Li nodded as he looked at Ling Ran and said, “If we’re taking the problem of continuation into consideration, we’ll have to do more than train a medical laboratory technician. You guys will also need to buy some newer equipment, or the results wouldn’t be as fast and accurate.”

“Hospitals from all over the province are sending equipment over to us this time. We’ll try our best to keep some.” Compared to purchasing equipment, it was way simpler to get equipment from other hospitals. Xiang Xueming had his own opinions about this.

“I can ask Yun Hua Hospital to send some medical consumables over.” Ling Ran had started using color indicator undergloves in Yun Hua Hospital a long time ago. But in Bazhaixiang, he had no choice but to wear two layers of ordinary gloves during scheduled surgeries. Now that the roads were usable, not only would this problem be solved, but he would also be able to purchase more underpants so that he could change into a new pair of underpants before every surgery.
“Quick lab tests, better cooperation, and improved occupational exposure...” Chief Physician Li concluded their discussion after he heard what Ling Ran said. His eyes slowly lit up.
With so many areas of responsibilities, he would be able to get more projects.
After the conversation ended, Ling Ran rose and left.
Without being aware of what he was doing, Chief Physician Li rose and saw him off. When he watched Ling Ran leave the Operating Area, he could not help but laugh.

Ling Ran was not in a rush to return to the operating theater. Since the roads were usable now, he reckoned that things would get better in the operating theater soon. Not only would more blood bags and drugs be sent over, but he would also have more choice of patients.
Ling Ran sauntered around with his hands in his pockets. He exited the hospital and watched the crowd, who were cheering, for a short while. He then followed the crowd to the center of the village.
Hurried footsteps rang out from behind him.
Soon, a pair of white sneakers appeared on the ground in front of Ling Ran.

“Are you going for a walk? Why don’t we go together?” Tian Qi’s smile was even more magnetic than those of the people in the crowd. In reality, the people who were cheering and walking around had slowed down, and they were also not as loud as before. All of them were looking at the center of the village.
Ling Ran flashed her an equally magnetic smile. He then rubbed his tummy and said, “I’m a bit hungry, let’s go and grab a bite.”

“Sure, we’re not as busy today, so we can purposely head out for good food,” Tian Qi said happily. It was as though she had forgotten that all of her meals and snacks lately were prepared by excellent chefs.
Ling Ran nodded slightly and walked beside Tian Qi. As he looked at the scenery and the person beside him, he could not help but to be in high spirits.

chapters.title: Chapter 878: Enjoy A Diversion
paragraphs: “The bleeding is controlled quite well today.”
“When I strip the liver and adrenal gland, I would break out in sweat, I didn’t expect you to do it so well, Doctor Wei.”
Two doctors from the provincial hospital surrounded Wei Jiayou and buttered him up as much as possible.

Wei Jiayou also looked excited. Although he always performed cardiovascular surgeries, which was more difficult and required more attention to detail, the sense of accomplishment from laparoscopic hepatectomy was similar.
In fact, since he wanted to compete with Ling Ran, it made Wei Jiayou become even more high spirited.

“Once you’re familiar with laparoscopy, when you do hepatectomy or cholecystectomy, it’s about the same.” Wei Jiayou praised himself from another perspective. Then, he took this chance to say, “Laparoscopy has an advantage. Its magnification function is very useful in hepatectomy. When it comes to the stripping of the adrenal gland, which you mentioned just now, when it’s magnified, it is actually much simpler than open abdominal surgery.”

“But bleeding control becomes more difficult. Normal people might not be able to control the bleeding like you do, Doctor Wei.” The two doctors from the provincial hospital who came to help were senior attending physicians, and they were about to be promoted to assistant lecturers. They were also considered to be outer sect disciples under Academician Di. They had developed medical skills, and their ability in buttering up to people was just as developed.
Compared to young doctors, they were less shameless, and they could butter up to the right things.

The one thing difficult about hepatectomy was how difficult it was to control the bleeding in the liver, and when it came to laparoscopic hepatectomy, this difficulty was magnified multiple times. When surgeons performing laparoscopic hepatectomy had to switch to laparotomies during the surgery, it was always because they cannot control the bleeding.
Both assistants praised Wei Jiayou’s bleeding control skill. Wei Jiayou was proud of that.
“Both of you have seen Ling Ran’s surgery too, right? What do you think of it compared to mine?” Wei Jiayou raised his head slightly.

He chose to support Bazhaixiang and also to stay temporarily at Bazhaixiang because he wanted to compete with Ling Ran. With his level and current age, his meaning of life was to keep competing with others.
Monkeys, gorillas, and even kindergarteners kept comparing themselves with their peers around them to ascertain their own status. This was an inborn instinct.
For a doctor, a comparison like this had more practical meaning.
Only first-class doctors could enjoy first-class resources. Only the best doctor could enjoy the best resources.
Wei Jiayou had long cast aside the desire for titles like that of an associate chief physician or chief physician. He wanted more, and so, his vision was even broader.
The two doctors from the provincial hospital felt a bit awkward.

They tried to size up how shameless each other were and compete with each other who was more shameless, and the winner first said, “Doctor Wei’s hepatectomy skill is suited to the local conditions, and that is something Doctor Ling cannot compare to.”
“Exactly. Doctor Wei did very well for today’s surgery.” The loser followed up quickly and said. They did not bother about their integrity anymore.
Wei Jiayou did not feel that there was anything wrong with their statement. He used to be praised by others. After he became the disciple of Academician Di, he was praised even more than ever.
“Yes. Do the two of you always observe Ling Ran’s surgeries at Yun Hua Hospital?” Wei Jiayou suddenly thought of this question.
“How can we? Everyone has work to do.” The shameless attending physician smiled and said, “But we will sometimes watch the livestream from Yunli Medical Company.”
Wei Jiayou knew about the livestreamed surgeried by Yunli Medical Company as well. He suddenly changed his mind and asked, “You guys always watch that?”
“Sometimes.”
“I’m sure both of you have a lot of work, right? Among the surgeries you watched, which surgeon appeared the most?”
Both attending physicians hesitated.
“Ling Ran?” Wei Jiayou was surprised. “Why?”

The shameless attending physician tried to explain, “Um... After all, we are from the General Surgery Department. Hepatectomy is one of the most high-end surgery types in the field of general surgery. And Ling Ran is quite famous for this.”

The shameless attending physician also added, “The hospitals in Changxi Province do quite acknowledge Ling Ran’s skills in hepatectomy. Doctor Wei, you’re a cardiologist at Beijing. You don’t walk down the same path as him.”

Wei Jiayou was not a fool. He chuckled, put his hands behind him, and said, “It’s fine, I’ll go and check out the surgeries performed by Ling Ran. It’s more convenient to observe it live than from streamed videos.”
The two attending physicians followed behind him and saw that Wei Jiayou walked like a ginseng baby without a red string tied to it . They could not help but sigh together.
“Our EQ is not sufficient.”
“Were we tactful enough?”

“Why should we be tactful? At this moment, we should just turn our backs against our consciousness and butter him up so much he’s covered in butter. At the very least, if we manage to butter him up, it won’t be a waste that we were sent here.”
Wei Jiayou found the operating theater and saw Zuo Cidian standing at the position of the chief surgeon.
Wei Jiayou was incredibly shocked. “You can perform surgery as well?”
Zuo Cidian looked up and saw Wei Jiayou. He could not help but sigh, “Doctor Wei, won’t the way you speak offend anyone in Beijing?”

Wei Jiayou was reminded of this fact, and he smiled in embarrassment. He quickly said, “I didn’t mean it. I just let myself run a little too loose when I’m here. Are you treating... a Colles’ fracture?”
“Yes. The patient was injured badly...”
“Colles’ fracture is considered an injury as well?” Wei Jiayou smiled. “Are you actually an orthopedist?”
Zuo Cidian sighed again. “Doctor Wei, what brought you here?”
“Oh, I’m looking for Ling Ran.”
“Doctor Ling is resting now.”
“Resting? Resting for what?” Wei Jiayou was even more shocked.
“Recently, the roads are all cleared, and there are other doctors who came over to help. It has been a long time since we ran out of hospital beds, and we have to distribute them as well...”
Zuo Cidian said lots of stuff, and Wei Jiayou finally understood the situation.
“Where is Ling Ran?” Wei Jiayou asked.
“Taking a walk, maybe?” Zuo Cidian replied.
This reply was against Wei Jiayou’s expectations.

Wei Jiayou could only think that if Ling Ran who was at the operating theater, he should be at the cafeteria, performing consultations or even bathing. But he could not think of Ling Ran... taking a walk.
“Where did he go for a walk? Aren’t there a group of people chasing after him?” Wei Jiayou said subconsciously. He then shook his head fiercely and asked, “Where is his exact location?”
“Why are you looking for Doctor Ling?” Zuo Cidian raised his head and looked at Wei Jiayou.
“About surgeries.”
Zuo Cidian waited for a few seconds before replying, “At Zhongzhai.”

Zhongzhai was a village at the border of Bazhaixiang. Since it was close to the geographical center of Bazhaixiang and it was not too far away from the main street of Bazhaixiang, it will only take half an hour to reach that place, and it can be considered as one of the scenic locations in Bazhaixiang.
Wei Jiayou ignored that and asked for a car before he drove to Zhongzhai.
The road heading to the center of Zhongzhai was only at the level of a village road. Along the way were huge and tall trees as well as mist, and it could make a person feel refreshed.

Wei Jiayou treated this excursion as a diversion to enjoy himself to get rid of all the frustration from how things did not go his way over the past few days. He even slowed down his driving speed to delay his time of arrival.
After half an hour, before he arrived in Zhongzhai, Wei Jiayou saw Ling Ran at a small platform at the top of a cliff.
It was impossible for him not to see Ling Ran.
A cement platform that was about half the size of a basketball court was now covered with a red carpet, and on its center were a table and chairs.
Ling Ran and Tian Qi sat at both ends of the table while looking at the sunset.
They were surrounded by green forest, and the mountain scenery around them lasted for miles. Around them were also dozens of servants and chefs, who were busy...
“This man is having a picnic? And it’s such a luxurious picnic...” Wei Jiayou mumbled to himself. His relaxed mind started to become conflicted again.

After half an hour, before he arrived in Zhongzhai, Wei Jiayou saw Ling Ran at a small platform at the top of a cliff.
It was impossible for him not to see Ling Ran.
A cement platform that was about half the size of a basketball court was now covered with a red carpet, and on its center were a table and chairs.
Ling Ran and Tian Qi sat at both ends of the table while looking at the sunset.
They were surrounded by green forest, and the mountain scenery around them lasted for miles.
Around them were also dozens of servants and chefs, who were busy...
“This man is having a picnic?
And it’s such a luxurious picnic...” Wei Jiayou mumbled to himself.
His relaxed mind started to become conflicted again.

chapters.title: Chapter 879: Sunset
paragraphs: “The scenery in Bazhaixiang is actually very beautiful.” Tian Qi looked at the sunset with a smile on her face. She then glanced at Ling Ran. She could not help but be in an extremely good mood. It was like every cell in her body was happy.

Ling Ran nodded slightly and said, “The average altitude of Bazhaixiang is relatively high, and the place gets sufficient rainfall. Hence, the plants grow in a pretty different environment compared to Yun Hua City.”
“But it’s very beautiful, isn’t it?”
“It’s very beautiful.” Ling Ran looked at Tian Qi.
Tian Qi flashed a sweet smile. She grabbed a glass of red wine and said, “Oh, by the way, I made this batch of red wine. Why don’t you give it a try and tell me if it’s nice?”
“I rarely drink any alcohol.” Even though Ling Ran said that, he still grabbed the wine glass before him and took a small sip.
The red wine was thick, and even though it was slightly bitter, it formed a rich taste together with the sweetness.
“Does it taste good?” Tian Qi was very concerned about Ling Ran’s opinion of the wine.
“It’s pretty good. The taste of tannin isn’t that strong.” Ling Ran swayed the wine glass skillfully.

“You said that you rarely drink any alcohol, but you do drink, don’t you?” Tian Qi was a clever woman, and she immediately realized something after pondering about Ling Ran’s words. “Is Madam Ling the one who taught you how to drink?”
“Yes.” Ling Ran smiled and nodded.
“Hm... if that’s the case, should I give Madam Ling some red wine? But... it might not be a very appropriate gift.” Tian Qi was conflicted.
Ling Ran lowered his head and started cutting his steak.

As usual, Chef Zhu was the one who grilled the steak today. It was a Brazillian Zebu, and it tasted very beefy. The Zebu had slimmed down a little after being reared in Yun Hua for a few months. However, it still tasted just as delicious. It had been grilled over blazing flames, and all of the juice was locked inside the meat.

Ling Ran cut his steak skilfully, and he cut himself a large chunk of beef. He placed the chunk of beef in his mouth and started chewing it. He was tired after performing surgeries for many consecutive days, and this was mainly mental fatigue. After this mouthful of steak, it was as if all the fatigue had dissipated.
For every few mouthfuls of steak Ling Ran ate, he would take a sip of wine. Soon, he finished the large chunk of ribeye steak.

Chef Zhu was wearing a tall toque, and he asked politely as he stood beside Ling Ran with his hands clasped behind his back, “Doctor Ling, do you want a New York strip steak? I’ve just finished grilling it.”
“Sure.” Ling Ran immediately agreed without bothering to put on a polite front. He was rather excited about the steak.

Three attendants walked over. One of them cleared Ling Ran’s plate, while another cleaned the table as well as the table cloth. The third attendant placed a New York strip steak on the table. There were some marks on the steak courtesy of the grill.

Compared with the juicy and tender ribeye steak, the New York strip steak, which was made with boneless sirloin, was more coarse and elastic. It was perfect to eat a New York strip steak after a ribeye steak, as the person eating it would not become tired of eating steak, and would also be able to taste the uniqueness of the steak.

Truth be told, the main attractions of both Brazillian steak and American steak were their juiciness and beefiness, as both kinds of steak were mainly made up of lean meat. Steaks made using Australian or Japanese wagyu beef were so greasy that people would get sick of them after eating half a pound of them. If a person were to eat a catty or two pounds of these at one go, he might not crave for steak again for the rest of his life.
In contrast to Australian and Japanese wagyu steak, New York strip steak was made out of more lean meat. Hence, it was more suitable for those with a big appetite.
The New York strip steak in front of Ling Ran was around 1.5 pounds. He felt tremendously satisfied as he paired it with a glass of red wine.

Tian Qi was done eating a while back. She held her glass of red wine and took slow sips. She glanced at the beautiful scenery, and then at Ling Ran. This filled her heart with happiness. At this moment, even though she was in Bazhaixiang, she found the scenery extremely beautiful, and she felt that this was the happiest place on earth.
“If a vacation home were built here, it should be a very comfortable place to stay in.” Tian Qi gazed down the cliff, and she was able to get a good view of the scenery below her.
Ling Ran followed Tian Qi’s gaze and did not disagree with what she said. “If the vacation home is easily accessible, I’ll give it a 70 out of 100.”
“Oh, is that so? This place is great, but it’s not unique enough.” Tian Qi then looked at Ling Ran and asked, “Doctor Ling, do you like vacation homes?”

“I’ve never been to one, but I don’t want to stay too far away from the hospital.” Ling Ran swallowed the beef in his mouth, and he looked like a lion who was swallowing its prey. He raised his head a little as he spoke.

Tian Qi nodded in agreement. “Yeah, it would be such a waste for you to spend time traveling when you could use that time to save patients’ life instead. But compared to other places in Changxi Province, the scenery in Bazhaixiang is really beautiful. If you travel in a straight line, it’s not too far from Yun Hua City either. If an expressway were built, this would be a pretty good place to stay.”
Tian Qi looked at her administrative secretary, who was standing not far away from her.

Her administrative secretary was an obedient-looking woman. She was wearing black-rimmed spectacles, a pair of flats, and old-fashioned office wear. She quickly made some notes on her laptop and said, “Right now, the leaders of Changxi Province welcome those who want to help rebuild Bazhaixiang very much. If we were to build a small housing area or a nursing home here, I reckon that reception would be good. Should I ask someone to make an analysis report?”
“Sure.” Tian Qi gave an affirmative answer.
The administrative secretary faded back into the background.
Tian Qi turned to look at Ling Ran again. She suddenly said in embarrassment, “Sorry, Doctor Ling. I could not help but talk about work.”
“It’s okay, I like work too.” Ling Ran raised his head to glance at her. He then continued cutting his steak.
Tian Qi flashed a smile that was as beautiful as the sunset.
By the time they were done with dinner, the sun had set almost completely.
Ling Ran and Tian Qi left in a helicopter. Two vans that were parked in the forest drove over to collect the cooking equipment, leftover ingredients, and the small amount of trash.

On the vans’ way back to the Bazhaixiang hospital branch, they even helped a driver out. The driver’s car had broken down in the middle of the road. Naturally, cars in Bazhaixiang were not that well-maintained.
After Ling Ran arrived at the hospital, he did not return to the operating theater. He glanced at his phone before he returned to his room to play a game on his phone.
After the roads that led to Yun Hua City became usable, Changping District Hospital’s Bazhaixiang hospital branch was flooded with doctors from all over the province who went there to help out.

Ling Ran never liked the crowd, and he hated crowded hospitals even more. Hence, at a time like this, he did not bother to join the legion of doctors in the hospital branch and squeeze into the operating theater.

After losing a few games, Ling Ran suppressed the desire to start a new game. He thought for a moment about what to do before opening the WeChat app on his phone. He sent a message to his treatment group’s chat group. [Summarize the evaluation of target lesions in the human liver.]
After he sent the message, Ling Ran covered himself with his blanket. He felt at ease as he went to sleep.
The following day, the Bazhaixiang hospital branch became even livelier than before. Naturally, fewer tasks were allocated to the Ling Treatment Group.

As Zuo Cidian was worried that Ling Ran would be unhappy, he waited for Ling Ran at the door and said, “All the patients now are basically just here for common illnesses. At most, there are some regulars who utilize the subsidy that’s being given now to seek treatment so that they could save some money. Two or three doctors would be enough to see to these patients. Right now, there are six or seven medical teams present, and there are around twenty or thirty doctors. There’s nothing much for us to do.”
Ling Ran nodded, but he corrected Zuo Cidian. “The patients who were transferred here will stay.”
Zuo Cidian shrugged. “They’re all from the same village. How many patients could there be? Why don’t you take the opportunity to rest for a few days?”

There were not many patients left, and the doctors from the medical teams who came after the roads were usable were extremely proactive as they fought to carry out all the available tasks. Truth be told, Lu Wenbin and the other members of the Ling Treatment Group were already extremely tired, and Zuo Cidian did not think that they would be able to perform better than the fresh manpower.
Ling Ran thought about it and said, “I’ll go and debride wounds at the emergency room, then.”

“Debridement... There aren’t many patients who need debridement. But you can go ahead if you’re bored,” Zuo Cidian said helplessly. There were almost ten thousand people in Yun Hua City, and whenever a person got hurt, their first choice would always be large hospitals such as Yun Hua Hospital. But in the Bazhaixiang hospital branch, it was well possible that there would not be any patient who sustained external injuries for days.

However, even in the Bazhaixiang hospital branch, the doctors who were there on the rescue mission did not like to treat patients with minor injuries in the emergency room. So, they would not fight for the task with Ling Ran.
Hence, Ling Ran headed to the emergency room, the same way he always did in Yun Hua Hospital. He sat and did nothing as he waited for patients to arrive.
Zuo Cidian stared ahead as he sat behind Ling Ran. He was ready to start daydreaming.
Right then, a middle-aged woman whose hand was wrapped using a towel arrived on a motorbike.
“Doctor!” the driver of the motorbike growled. He hopped down the motorbike and carried the middle-aged woman off the motorbike. He suddenly tripped, and both of them fell to the ground.
Everyone in the emergency room went silent for a moment.
Only then did a nurse push a gurney over. It took six people to put the patient on the gurney.
“How did she get hurt?” Ling Ran asked as he followed them into the reception hall.

“Our house is being renovated, and she accidentally got stabbed by the sharp end of a piece of wood.” The driver of the motorbike was around forty years old. He rested a hand on his waist as he panted.
“I’m going to remove the towel.” Ling Ran put on a pair of gloves and called a nurse over to help him out. He then started removing the towel.
That was when a reporter who was holding a camera walked over.

chapters.title: Chapter 880: 37/1
paragraphs: Chief Physician Li looked calm, but he was secretly excited when he welcomed the reporters from Yun Hua.
These reporters took to the trouble of coming to Bazhaixiang, and so, it was important for doctors to fight for the chance to promote themselves and spread what they were doing to the public.
For Chief Physician Li, the success of public health programs was even more dependent on the media and reporters.

However, society always expected medical doctors to hold themselves aloof from politics and material pursuits. In old times, experts in medicine always hid in the forest while they treated people. When they entered a big city like Beijing, the reviews on them would be immediately changed.
Chief Physician Li wanted to promote himself, but he did not want to make it too obvious because of his bashfulness, so it was actually very hard for him to put on the act.
He was not the only one being awkward, the other doctors also acted awkwardly.
They all fought hard for their chance to come to Bazhaixiang.
After working on so many things, reporters finally came to interview them, so everyone also wanted a chance.
Most of the doctors tried as hard as possible to perform their best.

Those who were capable of performing high-end surgeries would grab the chance to occupy the operating theater and display their skills. For some who were good at performing a particular surgery, the calculative ones would perform on the patients they had prepared before, while those who did not think beforehand eagerly wanted to immediately have a patient for them to work on.
The reporter and cameraman shot the scenes calmly, while the government staff who followed along seemed to be slightly bored.

This was not their first time doing something similar in a hospital, so they had seen such a similar scenario more than once. Once they had seen plenty of it, they naturally became less excited and more bored.
“Alright, thank you.” The reporter nodded at Chief Physician Li calmly.
Although the doctors worked hard to perform highly difficult surgeries, surgeries they were familiar with, interesting surgeries, or even complicated projects, they were all the same for reporters.
Chief Physician Li found himself unable to accept this, and he said, “Let me bring you around the place.”
“We can go around on our own.” The reporter pulled the cameraman along and wanted to leave.

“It’s fine, I’m familiar with the hospital.” How could Chief Physician Li be defeated by a few words? He continued to follow them while he eased their nonexisting anxiety of the chaos around them. “It’s too crowded in the hospital, and we have too many tasks on our hands right now. Oh yes, what kind of photos do you want to take?”

“The doctors will definitely be in the photos.” The reporter thought that Chief Physician Li wanted to ask about that, so he answered before the reporter said, “We want to find some events happening behind the scenes. We can’t just report perfect heroes, the readers won’t like it.”

“You’re right.” Chief Physician Li chuckled but thought, ‘With how newspapers operate nowadays, are you really searching for events behind the scenes? You just want to make those your main content, right?’
During the conversation, the trio went down the stairs. Then, they were blocked by Associate Chief Physician Deng, who heard about the arrival of the reporters.

The chief physician and associate chief physician from the provincial hospital did manage to stop the government staff and doctors from small hospitals, but the official reporter and cameraman pretended they did not see them and continued moving around in the small Bazhaixiang hospital branch.
As they walked around, they entered the emergency room.
When they saw Ling Ran, the cameraman naturally lifted his camera.
Nowadays, when someone filmed a movie, they would naturally look for good looking actors. Hence, when they interviewed people and ran into handsome doctors, they should naturally record it.
The reporter, who looked stern since the beginning, could not help but show a smile and slowed down his steps.
“This is Doctor Ling Ran, right?” The reporter asked Chief Physician Li, who was by his side.
Chief Physician Li smiled bitterly and said, “He is Doctor Ling.”
“He’s truly... very handsome.” The reporter covered his mouth and smiled. He looked really happy.
“Indeed.” What else could Chief Physician Li say?

“What is Doctor Ling doing now?” The reporter did not go forward immediately, but he stood at the back and wanted to know more about what was going on. Naturally, he had never acted this way. After all, the reporter did not bother about what sort of impression the doctors had of him.
Chief Physician Li secretly sighed before he craned his head to see that Ling Ran was already within the coverage of the camera. Then, he said to the reporter, “He is now performing a suture.”
“Do you mean suturing a wound?”
“Yes.”

“What are the difficulties and main points in this?” The reporter looked very serious, and he seemed to humbly request for knowledge. He looked even more earnest than the time he watched another surgeon cut a pancreas just now.
Chief Physician Li hummed before he watched Ling Ran perform a suture with a curved surgical needle. He then said to the reporter, “He’s just suturing a wound.”
“There are good and bad sides for suturing a wound, as well as easy and difficult aspects, right?”
“For Ling Ran?” Chief Physician Li smiled and said, “If you really want to know, good suturing will mean a good recovery. A small scar would also make the patient feel more comfortable. That’s it.”

“Oh, that’s good enough.” The reporter kept nodding. The previous surgery was too hard for him to understand. But now that they were talking about sutures alone, the reporter could understand it clearly.
Chief Physician Li felt helpless.
‘This is not a difficult skill, okay?

‘It would have been good if you behaved this way for every surgery, but just now, there was a major surgery involving four people, and here, Ling Ran is just suturing the arm for an elderly woman, but you didn’t react that way for that major surgery!’

“Doctor Ling, from what I know, you’re one of the doctors who entered Bazhaixiang earliest, and you have performed many major surgeries in Bazhaixiang. But why are you here in the emergency room performing a small surgery like suturing?” The reporter came to Ling Ran at this time and asked a question, but no one could guess his intentions for asking it.
Chief Physician Li felt anxious. ‘Is this guy here to cause trouble?’
However, Ling Ran continued suturing without raising his head, and he said, “Since the patient has been wounded by a woodworking tool, she needs a suture.”

“Hmm?” The reporter was stunned, then he shook his head and said, “Doctor Ling, I mean you’re now a well-known doctor for major surgeries, so why are you still willing to perform such a minor surgery in the emergency room?”
Ling Ran cast a puzzled glance at the reporter and asked, “Then, should I just let the patient bleed?”

The reporter was a little baffled by Ling Ran’s answer. He could not say that Ling Ran’s answer was not relevant to his question, but his answer was not totally reasonable either, and perhaps a language teacher would not be pleased with his answer.
The reporter took a deep breath and asked again, “You can pass this kind of minor surgeries to other doctors, right?”
“Yeah.”
“But you still decided to do it yourself?”
“Yes.”
The reporter felt slightly relieved that they were finally having a normal conversation, so he continued to ask, “Is there any reason behind it?”
However, Ling Ran was slightly annoyed now. ‘Do I need a reason to perform surgery?’
Ling Ran stopped working and took a glance at the reporter, then he looked at the camera again and said, “Because I encountered a patient who requires me to treat her.”
“Because you encountered a patient?” The reporter became stunned again. He suddenly felt the interview today was incredibly tiring.
The cameraman by the side, Chief Physician Li, and Associate Chief Physician Deng were also exhausted by just listening to the conversation, but they remained quiet without making any noise.

“So... your reason is that you encountered a patient, so you want to treat her, right?” The reporter decided to use his specialty and started to make up a story. “When you run into a patient at the disaster response site, you need to give him or her treatment. You don’t need to consider your level and skills, you just need to the patient. Is that so?”
Ling Ran glanced at the reporter like he would when he looked at a Zebu. Then, he lowered his head and continued suturing.
In just a few minutes, the patient’s wound on her arm was closed by the surgical silk suture.
“Dressing.” Ling Ran performed a simple checkup and cleaned the wound before he gave up his spot.
At this time, a light shone in front of him
[Mission Completed: Perfect Surgery (37/1)]
[Reward: Basic Treasure Chest]
Ling Ran’s expression changed a little. A debridement and suture surgery like this was considered a mission as well?
*Clap clap clap clap*
The reporter clapped and praised Ling Ran. “Well done, Doctor Ling. Smile for the camera, please.”
Therefore, Ling Ran showed a smile that fulfilled the expectations of society.
The reporter even smiled like a flower. His grip around his tie loosened.

Chief Physician Li wanted to promote himself, but he did not want to make it too obvious because of his bashfulness, so it was actually very hard for him to put on the act.
He was not the only one being awkward, the other doctors also acted awkwardly.
They all fought hard for their chance to come to Bazhaixiang.
After working on so many things, reporters finally came to interview them, so everyone also wanted a chance.
Most of the doctors tried as hard as possible to perform their best.
Those who were capable of performing high-end surgeries would grab the chance to occupy the operating theater and display their skills.

For some who were good at performing a particular surgery, the calculative ones would perform on the patients they had prepared before, while those who did not think beforehand eagerly wanted to immediately have a patient for them to work on.
The reporter and cameraman shot the scenes calmly, while the government staff who followed along seemed to be slightly bored.
This was not their first time doing something similar in a hospital, so they had seen such a similar scenario more than once.
Once they had seen plenty of it, they naturally became less excited and more bored.
“Alright, thank you.” The reporter nodded at Chief Physician Li calmly.
Although the doctors worked hard to perform highly difficult surgeries, surgeries they were familiar with, interesting surgeries, or even complicated projects, they were all the same for reporters.
Chief Physician Li found himself unable to accept this, and he said, “Let me bring you around the place.”
“We can go around on our own.” The reporter pulled the cameraman along and wanted to leave.
“It’s fine, I’m familiar with the hospital.” How could Chief Physician Li be defeated by a few words?
He continued to follow them while he eased their nonexisting anxiety of the chaos around them.
“It’s too crowded in the hospital, and we have too many tasks on our hands right now.
Oh yes, what kind of photos do you want to take?”

“The doctors will definitely be in the photos.” The reporter thought that Chief Physician Li wanted to ask about that, so he answered before the reporter said, “We want to find some events happening behind the scenes.
We can’t just report perfect heroes, the readers won’t like it.”
“You’re right.” Chief Physician Li chuckled but thought, ‘With how newspapers operate nowadays, are you really searching for events behind the scenes?
You just want to make those your main content, right?’
During the conversation, the trio went down the stairs.
Then, they were blocked by Associate Chief Physician Deng, who heard about the arrival of the reporters.

The chief physician and associate chief physician from the provincial hospital did manage to stop the government staff and doctors from small hospitals, but the official reporter and cameraman pretended they did not see them and continued moving around in the small Bazhaixiang hospital branch.
As they walked around, they entered the emergency room.
When they saw Ling Ran, the cameraman naturally lifted his camera.
Nowadays, when someone filmed a movie, they would naturally look for good looking actors.
Hence, when they interviewed people and ran into handsome doctors, they should naturally record it.
The reporter, who looked stern since the beginning, could not help but show a smile and slowed down his steps.
“This is Doctor Ling Ran, right?” The reporter asked Chief Physician Li, who was by his side.
Chief Physician Li smiled bitterly and said, “He is Doctor Ling.”
“He’s truly... very handsome.” The reporter covered his mouth and smiled.
He looked really happy.
“Indeed.” What else could Chief Physician Li say?
“What is Doctor Ling doing now?” The reporter did not go forward immediately, but he stood at the back and wanted to know more about what was going on.
Naturally, he had never acted this way.
After all, the reporter did not bother about what sort of impression the doctors had of him.
Chief Physician Li secretly sighed before he craned his head to see that Ling Ran was already within the coverage of the camera.
Then, he said to the reporter, “He is now performing a suture.”
“Do you mean suturing a wound?”
“Yes.”
“What are the difficulties and main points in this?” The reporter looked very serious, and he seemed to humbly request for knowledge.
He looked even more earnest than the time he watched another surgeon cut a pancreas just now.
Chief Physician Li hummed before he watched Ling Ran perform a suture with a curved surgical needle.
He then said to the reporter, “He’s just suturing a wound.”
“There are good and bad sides for suturing a wound, as well as easy and difficult aspects, right?”
“For Ling Ran?” Chief Physician Li smiled and said, “If you really want to know, good suturing will mean a good recovery.
A small scar would also make the patient feel more comfortable.
That’s it.”
“Oh, that’s good enough.” The reporter kept nodding.
The previous surgery was too hard for him to understand.
But now that they were talking about sutures alone, the reporter could understand it clearly.
Chief Physician Li felt helpless.
‘This is not a difficult skill, okay?

‘It would have been good if you behaved this way for every surgery, but just now, there was a major surgery involving four people, and here, Ling Ran is just suturing the arm for an elderly woman, but you didn’t react that way for that major surgery!’
“Doctor Ling, from what I know, you’re one of the doctors who entered Bazhaixiang earliest, and you have performed many major surgeries in Bazhaixiang.

But why are you here in the emergency room performing a small surgery like suturing?” The reporter came to Ling Ran at this time and asked a question, but no one could guess his intentions for asking it.
Chief Physician Li felt anxious.
‘Is this guy here to cause trouble?’
However, Ling Ran continued suturing without raising his head, and he said, “Since the patient has been wounded by a woodworking tool, she needs a suture.”

“Hmm?” The reporter was stunned, then he shook his head and said, “Doctor Ling, I mean you’re now a well-known doctor for major surgeries, so why are you still willing to perform such a minor surgery in the emergency room?”
Ling Ran cast a puzzled glance at the reporter and asked, “Then, should I just let the patient bleed?”
The reporter was a little baffled by Ling Ran’s answer.
He could not say that Ling Ran’s answer was not relevant to his question, but his answer was not totally reasonable either, and perhaps a language teacher would not be pleased with his answer.
The reporter took a deep breath and asked again, “You can pass this kind of minor surgeries to other doctors, right?”
“Yeah.”
“But you still decided to do it yourself?”
“Yes.”
The reporter felt slightly relieved that they were finally having a normal conversation, so he continued to ask, “Is there any reason behind it?”
However, Ling Ran was slightly annoyed now.
‘Do I need a reason to perform surgery?’
Ling Ran stopped working and took a glance at the reporter, then he looked at the camera again and said, “Because I encountered a patient who requires me to treat her.”
“Because you encountered a patient?” The reporter became stunned again.
He suddenly felt the interview today was incredibly tiring.
The cameraman by the side, Chief Physician Li, and Associate Chief Physician Deng were also exhausted by just listening to the conversation, but they remained quiet without making any noise.
“So... your reason is that you encountered a patient, so you want to treat her, right?” The reporter decided to use his specialty and started to make up a story.
“When you run into a patient at the disaster response site, you need to give him or her treatment.
You don’t need to consider your level and skills, you just need to the patient.
Is that so?”
Ling Ran glanced at the reporter like he would when he looked at a Zebu.
Then, he lowered his head and continued suturing.
In just a few minutes, the patient’s wound on her arm was closed by the surgical silk suture.
“Dressing.” Ling Ran performed a simple checkup and cleaned the wound before he gave up his spot.
At this time, a light shone in front of him
[Mission Completed: Perfect Surgery (37/1)]
[Reward: Basic Treasure Chest]
Ling Ran’s expression changed a little.
A debridement and suture surgery like this was considered a mission as well?
*Clap clap clap clap*
The reporter clapped and praised Ling Ran.
“Well done, Doctor Ling.
Smile for the camera, please.”
Therefore, Ling Ran showed a smile that fulfilled the expectations of society.
The reporter even smiled like a flower.
His grip around his tie loosened.

chapters.title: Chapter 881: Elevation of Skill
paragraphs: After Ling Ran was done carrying out debridement and suturing on a patient, he went back to his seat to rest.
The reporter dragged the cameraman along as he walked toward Ling Ran. They started talking about everything and nothing at the same time.
Of course, he was the sole person talking, Ling Ran did not even bother talking.
Zuo Cidian noticed that it was almost time, so he walked over to interrupt them. He promised the reporter that he would give him some information, and the latter finally left reluctantly.
Chief Physician Li was envious and sad at the same time when he saw their interaction.

He no longer had the chance to become the department director of the General Surgery Department of Yun Hua Provincial Hospital. Hence, he had given up and gotten involved in public health instead. However, it was impossible for him not to start fantasizing about things when he saw a reporter.

While it was already impossible for him to become the department director of the General Surgery Department, Chief Physician Li did not mind becoming the department director of a newly established Department of Public Health.

After working in the field for many years, different doctors might have different aims in life. But their work aspirations would be almost the same. Was there any doctor who did not dream of becoming a department director?
Even though most doctors would not get this opportunity until the end of their careers, a chief physician like Chief Physician Li was only one step away from becoming a department director.
It was a shame that he did not really have anyone backing him up.
Chief Physician Li watched as the reporter left the emergency room, and he could do nothing but let out a soft sigh.

The media could have done a good job of backing him up. However, the reporter did not seem interested in him, and even if the reporter were to force himself to write an article about him, it would be meaningless.
“I’ll be taking my leave, then.” Chief Physician Li did not feel like staying in the emergency room and watching a young doctor like Ling Ran work.

“Let’s head out together,” Associate Chief Physician Deng said with a smile. He was also a little emotional. However, as the young and capable leader of a treatment group, he still had a bright future ahead of him. Hence, he was not as despondent as chief physician Li.
Lu Wenbin, who was standing beside Ling Ran and flexing his muscles, sighed softly too. He relaxed his muscles, and he looked like a buff doctor.
“Doctor Ling, there’re no more patients in the waiting room. Do you want to take a short rest?” Zuo Cidian handed Ling Ran a bottle of mineral water and whispered.
Ling Ran was a little surprised. “I’ve only treated one patient, and we’ve now run out of patients?”

“Yeah, there are no more patients. There was a patient with a stomach ache just now, and he was already treated.” Zuo Cidian flashed a wan smile. Doctors like Ling Ran who began their career in a tertiary Grade A hospital might find this situation, where there were more doctors compared to patients, weird. However, this was basically what Zuo Cidian encountered every day during the first half of his career.

Ling Ran dejectedly whipped out his phone. He thought about it for a moment and decided to open the Ling Treatment Group’s WeChat group. He asked everyone a question. [What should be done during the preoperative period for patients with chronic Achilles tendon rupture?]
The doctors in the Ling Treatment Group could choose to give a long or short answer, and this was just the right question to ask them under the current circumstances.
Ling Ran was very satisfied with the question he came up with. He felt more at ease as he continued to play with his phone.
He played a game, and as expected, he lost. Ling Ran did not immediately start another game. Instead, he started pondering about things.
He was thinking about his “Perfect Surgery” mission.

It was relatively difficult to achieve perfection when it came to major surgeries like hepatectomy, and it was naturally easier to do so with minor surgeries. However, since the reward for the mission was only a Basic Treasure Chest, Ling Ran was not willing to spend too much energy on the mission.
It was not like he was looking down on Basic Treasure Chests, but lately, Basic Treasure Chests rarely gave him anything great.
When Ling Ran thought of this, he waved, and 37 basic treasure chests immediately appeared before him.
He had managed to perform 37 perfect surgeries, but he had opened none of the Basic Treasure Chests he received.

On one hand, it was because Ling Ran had way too many bottles of Energy Serum in his inventory. On the other hand, he would like to accumulate more Basic Treasure Chests in case he needed them at a later date.
But after receiving a notification regarding the mission right now, Ling Ran had the urge to open his Basic Treasure Chests.
There was no need to hesitate before opening Basic Treasure Chests, anyway, and 37 happened to be a prime number. Ling Ran waved and opened all the Basic Treasure Chests.
An array of... Energy Serums appeared before him. There was no surprise at all in that.
“Give me 37 more Basic Treasure Chests,” Ling Ran muttered internally, and 37 shiny Basic Treasure Chests appeared before him.
They opened to reveal another batch of Energy Serums.
“Thirty-seven more,” Ling Ran requested again.
The system gave him 37 more Basic Treasure Chests.
He repeated the same process four times before a skill book showed up.
It was a Single Skill Book, and he obtained a skill branch—Gastrointestinal Perforation Repair (Master Level).
“The probability of obtaining a skill book is a little low.” Ling Ran raised his chin. He was not very satisfied, and he did not plan to open more Basic Treasure Chests.

Ling Ran did not possess any skills related to the intestine right now, and Gastrointestinal Perforation Repair changed that. However, Ling Ran had no intention of carrying out intestinal surgery. This skill would most probably be a backup, and Ling Ran reckoned that he would never put it to use.

After opening four batches of Basic Treasure Chests, Ling Ran was left with fewer than 1,000 Basic Treasure Chests. He now had a total of 962 Basic Treasure Chests, and most of them Sincere Gratitude Basic Treasure Chests. Only a small part of them was from missions, and the number of Peers’ Admiration Basic Treasure Chests was about the same.
Ling Ran did the math, and he felt that he should save some Basic Treasure Chests for later. It was not easy to collect 1,000 Basic Treasure Chests.
“Where’s Yu Yuan?” Ling Ran looked around and realized that everyone was already getting started with the paperwork. Hence, he prepared to do some paperwork too.
Yu Yuan craned her head out from behind a corner.
“Let’s write a research paper.” Ling Ran squeezed some alcohol-based hand sanitizer onto his hand. He rubbed his hands and switched on his laptop.
Yu Yuan hummed in acknowledgment and asked, “What kind of research paper would you like to write?”
“Since we’ve been carrying out hepatectomy lately, I have some ideas,” Ling Ran said as he thought about it.
Yu Yuan immediately switched on her laptop and said, “We do have quite a number of hepatectomy cases.”

“I think that the classification regarding ways to deal with hepatectomy done using a laparoscope, via a small incision, or via a big incision can be further fine-tuned,” Ling Ran described his thoughts.

Ren Qi, who came from a county hospital, was sitting beside them right now. He was writing medical records with his laptop propped up on his belly, which was of above-average size. He was in a little bit of a daze.
‘Are you guys intending to write a research paper because you’re bored?
‘Do you guys get any kind of cases you guys want?
‘Aren’t you boasting a little too much right now?
‘When will my life be this great?’
Ren Qi was listening closely to their conversation. Ling Ran suddenly changed the topic and talked about a new idea.
“We can write a standalone research paper about hepatectomy done via small incisions.
“Since the current trend is still to carry out hepatectomy using a laparoscope and via large incisions, we should have accumulated quite a number of cases lately.”
Ling Ran described his thought process as he spoke, and he made some notes on his laptop.
After carrying out surgeries for so many consecutive days, there were a lot of ideas in Ling Ran’s mind.

These ideas were different before Ling Ran mentally sorted them out and put them to paper. However, once he decided to materialize these ideas into words, he had to put in another round of hard work and think long and hard.
“Elevation of skill. Perfect Level hepatectomy is achieved.” At some point in time, the system’s voice rang out in Ling Ran’s mind.

chapters.title: Chapter 882: Level Two Skill Book
paragraphs: Hepatectomy was considered one of the top surgical skills out there.
Previously, Ling Ran spent more of his time actually operating on patients. Even though he had been writing research papers, as a whole, he spent more of his time doing rather than thinking.
Never had he expected that by making notes when he was free, his hepatectomy skills would be elevated.
Before this, when he only possessed Master Level Hepatectomy, he was already capable of carrying out freelance surgeries all over Changxi Province. Now that he possessed Perfect Level Hepatectomy...
Ling Ran immediately asked internally, “System, what is my ranking right now when it comes to hepatectomy?”
“You possess Perfect Level Hepatectomy. You rank 5th in the world, 2nd in China, and 1st in Changxi Province...” The system gave a very quick answer.
Ling Ran arched an eyebrow.

He still remembered that the first perfect level skill he possessed was Perfect Level Barehanded Bleeding Control. But at that time, he did not even rank within the top hundred in the world for that, and he only ranked 13th in the country. Comparatively, Perfect Level Hepatectomy seemed to carry more weight.
Next, another notification from the system appeared.
[Reward: Self-Improvement]
[Reason for Reward: Obtained “Perfect Level Hepatectomy” courtesy of your own practice]
[Reward: Level Two Skill Book]
A skill book with golden rims appeared amid a ball of blue light. It was sparkling.
Ling Ran opened it without hesitation.
[Level Two Skill Book: Elevates a Basic Skill to Perfect Level]
Next, the six basic surgical skills appeared on the title page of the book. The words were sparkling.
[Exposure]
[Incision]
[Separation]
[Bleeding Control]
[Suturing]
[Drainage]

Ling Ran immediately understood that this meant he did not need to make any further choices after he selected one of the six basic skills and that a Level Two Skill Book allowed him to elevate one of the basic skills to the perfect level. That included all the skill branches.
But Ling Ran was hesitant.
Prior to that, he had obtained Barehanded Bleeding Control and Hemostasis by Heat via Level One Skill Books. After that, he had also chosen Separation of Tissues, which fell under Separation.
Ling Ran could pretty much carry out hepatectomy so well to the point of perfect level because he had the help of those perfect level skills.
The two bleeding control methods allowed Ling Ran to take risks and carry out all forms of hepatectomy. This also greatly lowered the risk of surgery.
As for the Separation of Tissues, it allowed him to navigate the most important aspect of hepatectomy smoothly.
Even a small skill branch within a basic skill could bring about such a great difference. How would things be like to be able to master an entire basic skill?
First, Ling Ran looked at Bleeding Control and Incision.
Bleeding control had always been important to a surgeon. The better the surgeon was at bleeding control, the lower the probability of patients dying on the operating table.

Ling Ran had already obtained two skill branches within Bleeding Control, and if he were to select Bleeding Control now and master all the skill branches, it was not like the system would give him two Level One Skill Books in return.

An incision was slightly different compared to separation. Incisions meant the cutting of tissues without complete removal. One example was incisions made during open abdominal surgery. Aside from that, separations did not always require a scalpel. Sometimes, tissues could be pulled off using a surgeon’s bare hands.
Compared with Separation, where Ling Ran had already obtained a skill branch from, he felt that Incision would be able to elevate his abilities to a greater extent.
After he thought about it, Ling Ran’s gaze fell on Exposure.

As the saying went, “It only takes five years to make a good surgeon, but a surgeon needs ten years to become good at exposure.” Even excellent surgeons like Ling Ran could not become good at exposure within two or three years after starting their career.

Aside from this, the route and mode of exposure for different kinds of surgery were different. If Ling Ran only had a Level One Skill Book now, he would need to choose between Bone Exposure, Liver Exposure, Skull Exposure, and others.
However, with a Level Two Skill Book, he could master all of them...
Ling Ran did not spend too much time hesitating. He clicked on Exposure.
In a flash, a large amount of information entered Ling Ran’s brain.
Ling Ran swayed a little as he sat on his chair.
“Doctor Ling?” Yu Yuan asked vigilantly. Ling Ran’s body was extremely huge compared to hers. Hence, it seemed to her as if Ling Ran had swayed a lot.

“I’m okay. Hmm... we were talking about classification of hepatectomies done via large incisions, weren’t we? I feel like we can make some changes to the part about thoracoabdominal incisions.” As Ling Ran stared at the screen of his laptop, there were some changes to his thought process.
Yu Yuan looked like an obedient tabby cat. She hummed in acknowledgment and started to type on the keyboard with her “paws”.
Ling Ran also made some notes on his laptop as he pondered.
The emergency room became quiet.

The doctors who had something to do were using all their strength to type so that they appeared hardworking. The doctors who had nothing to do pretended that they had something to do. As they could put their full focus on putting on an act, they seemed even more hardworking than those who actually had something to do.

Even the money plant on the windowsill was pretending to look very healthy. Its leaves swayed with the light breeze, and it looked like a buff guy who had just done a set of fifteen squats. It looked like it had muscles as hard as that of a zombie’s, and its stem was trembling so violently that it was as if it was suffering from Parkinson’s disease.
*Creak*
The old-fashioned double door which had not been repainted for a long time was opened in a hurry.
The department director of the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery of Yun Hua City’s Sixth People’s Hospital, Song Shang entered the emergency room.

Song Shang had invited Ling Ran over for freelance surgeries twice, and one of them was for somebody he knew. That surgery was held in Yun Hua City’s Sixth People’s Hospital. Another time, it was when a patient was suffering from a major hemorrhage. He had called Ling Ran over to help out.
Compared to other doctors who he had only met once or twice, Song Shang knew Ling Ran pretty well.

However, Song Shang was not in the mood to make small talk. He looked around, and when he saw that there was no patient present, he immediately said, “Doctor Ling, the liver of one of my patients was accidentally sliced, and he’s bleeding nonstop right now. Can you come over to take a look?”
“The liver was accidentally sliced?” Ling Ran was extremely dumbfounded when he heard what Song Shang said.

“Sigh... This subordinate of mine is an idiot. He’s always in a hurry. It was just a simple bile duct surgery.” Song Shang covered his face in embarrassment. He was in disbelief over how incompetent his subordinate was. If it were not for the fact that he was afraid that the patient would die on the operating table, Song Shang would not have asked for help.
“Has the patient lost a lot of blood?” Ling Ran stood up as he spoke.

“It’s almost 80 ounces now,” Song Shang uttered a white lie. In reality, by the time he headed over, the patient had lost around 100 ounces of blood. However, he lowered the figure as he was worried that Ling Ran would not want to help.
Ling Ran nodded. After he put on a pair of scrubs, he strode toward the operating theater.
Song Shang followed him and thanked him as he explained the situation.
It was a very common occurrence in every hospital for doctors to ask for help from other surgeons during surgery.
The weak doctors would ask for help, and the excellent doctors would save the day. This was always how things went.
Ling Ran arrived at the operating theater in a hurry. He quickly washed his hands and got changed before he walked over to the operating theater.
The young doctor who was performing bleeding control had both of his hands soaked in blood. He looked lost, and he did not respond when he saw his department director as well as Ling Ran
“How much blood has the patient lost?” Ling Ran asked the anesthetist directly.
“A hundred and eight ounces,” the anesthetist said.
Ling Ran nodded. The patient was considered to be in a pretty critical condition to have lost this much blood. If they were not careful about it, the patient would end up in the morgue.
“Make way for Doctor Ling,” Song Shang reminded the young doctor, who was in a daze.
“There’s no need for that.” Ling Ran went opposite the young doctor and looked down at the patient’s abdominal cavity. He slowly said, “We will control the bleeding together.”
Song Shang went over to stand beside Ling Ran. He nodded a few times and reprimanded his subordinate. “Hurry up and thank Doctor Ling for giving you a chance to correct your mistake.”

Ling Ran hummed softly in acknowledgment. He then slowly extended his hand into the patient’s abdominal cavity.

sentences.text: Hepatectomy was considered one of the top surgical skills out there.
Previously, Ling Ran spent more of his time actually operating on patients.
Even though he had been writing research papers, as a whole, he spent more of his time doing rather than thinking.
Never had he expected that by making notes when he was free, his hepatectomy skills would be elevated.
Before this, when he only possessed Master Level Hepatectomy, he was already capable of carrying out freelance surgeries all over Changxi Province.
Now that he possessed Perfect Level Hepatectomy...
Ling Ran immediately asked internally, “System, what is my ranking right now when it comes to hepatectomy?”
“You possess Perfect Level Hepatectomy.
You rank 5th in the world, 2nd in China, and 1st in Changxi Province...” The system gave a very quick answer.
Ling Ran arched an eyebrow.
He still remembered that the first perfect level skill he possessed was Perfect Level Barehanded Bleeding Control.
But at that time, he did not even rank within the top hundred in the world for that, and he only ranked 13th in the country.
Comparatively, Perfect Level Hepatectomy seemed to carry more weight.
Next, another notification from the system appeared.
[Reward: Self-Improvement]
[Reason for Reward: Obtained “Perfect Level Hepatectomy” courtesy of your own practice]
[Reward: Level Two Skill Book]
A skill book with golden rims appeared amid a ball of blue light.
It was sparkling.
Ling Ran opened it without hesitation.
[Level Two Skill Book: Elevates a Basic Skill to Perfect Level]
Next, the six basic surgical skills appeared on the title page of the book.
The words were sparkling.
[Exposure]
[Incision]
[Separation]
[Bleeding Control]
[Suturing]
[Drainage]

Ling Ran immediately understood that this meant he did not need to make any further choices after he selected one of the six basic skills and that a Level Two Skill Book allowed him to elevate one of the basic skills to the perfect level.
That included all the skill branches.
But Ling Ran was hesitant.
Prior to that, he had obtained Barehanded Bleeding Control and Hemostasis by Heat via Level One Skill Books.
After that, he had also chosen Separation of Tissues, which fell under Separation.
Ling Ran could pretty much carry out hepatectomy so well to the point of perfect level because he had the help of those perfect level skills.
The two bleeding control methods allowed Ling Ran to take risks and carry out all forms of hepatectomy.
This also greatly lowered the risk of surgery.
As for the Separation of Tissues, it allowed him to navigate the most important aspect of hepatectomy smoothly.
Even a small skill branch within a basic skill could bring about such a great difference.
How would things be like to be able to master an entire basic skill?
First, Ling Ran looked at Bleeding Control and Incision.
Bleeding control had always been important to a surgeon.
The better the surgeon was at bleeding control, the lower the probability of patients dying on the operating table.

Ling Ran had already obtained two skill branches within Bleeding Control, and if he were to select Bleeding Control now and master all the skill branches, it was not like the system would give him two Level One Skill Books in return.
An incision was slightly different compared to separation.
Incisions meant the cutting of tissues without complete removal.
One example was incisions made during open abdominal surgery.
Aside from that, separations did not always require a scalpel.
Sometimes, tissues could be pulled off using a surgeon’s bare hands.
Compared with Separation, where Ling Ran had already obtained a skill branch from, he felt that Incision would be able to elevate his abilities to a greater extent.
After he thought about it, Ling Ran’s gaze fell on Exposure.

As the saying went, “It only takes five years to make a good surgeon, but a surgeon needs ten years to become good at exposure.” Even excellent surgeons like Ling Ran could not become good at exposure within two or three years after starting their career.
Aside from this, the route and mode of exposure for different kinds of surgery were different.
If Ling Ran only had a Level One Skill Book now, he would need to choose between Bone Exposure, Liver Exposure, Skull Exposure, and others.
However, with a Level Two Skill Book, he could master all of them...
Ling Ran did not spend too much time hesitating.
He clicked on Exposure.
In a flash, a large amount of information entered Ling Ran’s brain.
Ling Ran swayed a little as he sat on his chair.
“Doctor Ling?” Yu Yuan asked vigilantly.
Ling Ran’s body was extremely huge compared to hers.
Hence, it seemed to her as if Ling Ran had swayed a lot.
“I’m okay.
Hmm... we were talking about classification of hepatectomies done via large incisions, weren’t we?
I feel like we can make some changes to the part about thoracoabdominal incisions.” As Ling Ran stared at the screen of his laptop, there were some changes to his thought process.
Yu Yuan looked like an obedient tabby cat.
She hummed in acknowledgment and started to type on the keyboard with her “paws”.
Ling Ran also made some notes on his laptop as he pondered.
The emergency room became quiet.
The doctors who had something to do were using all their strength to type so that they appeared hardworking.
The doctors who had nothing to do pretended that they had something to do.
As they could put their full focus on putting on an act, they seemed even more hardworking than those who actually had something to do.
Even the money plant on the windowsill was pretending to look very healthy.
Its leaves swayed with the light breeze, and it looked like a buff guy who had just done a set of fifteen squats.
It looked like it had muscles as hard as that of a zombie’s, and its stem was trembling so violently that it was as if it was suffering from Parkinson’s disease.
*Creak*
The old-fashioned double door which had not been repainted for a long time was opened in a hurry.
The department director of the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery of Yun Hua City’s Sixth People’s Hospital, Song Shang entered the emergency room.
Song Shang had invited Ling Ran over for freelance surgeries twice, and one of them was for somebody he knew.
That surgery was held in Yun Hua City’s Sixth People’s Hospital.
Another time, it was when a patient was suffering from a major hemorrhage.
He had called Ling Ran over to help out.
Compared to other doctors who he had only met once or twice, Song Shang knew Ling Ran pretty well.
However, Song Shang was not in the mood to make small talk.
He looked around, and when he saw that there was no patient present, he immediately said, “Doctor Ling, the liver of one of my patients was accidentally sliced, and he’s bleeding nonstop right now.
Can you come over to take a look?”
“The liver was accidentally sliced?” Ling Ran was extremely dumbfounded when he heard what Song Shang said.
“Sigh...
This subordinate of mine is an idiot.
He’s always in a hurry.
It was just a simple bile duct surgery.” Song Shang covered his face in embarrassment.
He was in disbelief over how incompetent his subordinate was.
If it were not for the fact that he was afraid that the patient would die on the operating table, Song Shang would not have asked for help.
“Has the patient lost a lot of blood?” Ling Ran stood up as he spoke.
“It’s almost 80 ounces now,” Song Shang uttered a white lie.
In reality, by the time he headed over, the patient had lost around 100 ounces of blood.
However, he lowered the figure as he was worried that Ling Ran would not want to help.
Ling Ran nodded.
After he put on a pair of scrubs, he strode toward the operating theater.
Song Shang followed him and thanked him as he explained the situation.

Only then did the young doctor seem like he had regained his senses.
He quickly said, “Thank you, Doctor Ling.”
Ling Ran hummed softly in acknowledgment.
