“Stop looking and carry on with your own tasks.”
“Why are you watching?
Haven’t you seen burn patients before?”
“If you want to help out with the burn patients, you can stay for a night shift.
We’ll reward you with some fruits.”
Some of the patients’ family members in the emergency room also took the initiative to ask their family members to disperse.
In Chinese hospitals, it was unavoidable that patients’ family members had to carry out a lot of extra and irrelevant tasks.
And because of this, the hospitals got to save on manpower.
But this resulted in extra chaos.
Meanwhile, in the wards, the longer a patient stayed in the hospital, the more familiar his family members were with the hospital.
It was to the point that they would even see life in the hospital as part of their life, just like how patients had no choice but to see their illnesses as part of their body.
It was not a pleasing choice, because there were no other options for them.
There were always regular patients and their family members in the emergency room.
Nowadays, it was harder to get a hospital bed in a tertiary Grade A hospital compared to f*cking an internet celebrity, and it was more expensive too.
Comparatively, it was much easier to obtain a hospital bed in the emergency room.
At least, patients who were ill but not in a critical condition could just call an ambulance and be sent to the emergency room.
This was what many regular patients often did.
And today, the hospital beds in the emergency room were more scarce than usual.
A few resident doctors furrowed their eyebrows as they tried to persuade a few patients whose conditions were not too serious to leave.
They also transferred even more patients to other departments so that those departments could worry about those patients.
At a time like this, departments that were not usually willing to take in regular patients had no choice but to put on a nice facade and take in a patient or two.
Hence, the emergency room was able to free up some space.
For that purpose, Zuo Cidian talked so much that his tongue became thinner.
At that moment, however, Huo Congjun did not emerge again.
He was fully focused on the two burn patients whom they had just taken in.
Aside from making sure that their vitals were fine, the doctors also had to monitor their amount of urine and fluid transfused as well as prevent infection.
It was an extremely complicated task.
Ling Ran, who was in the emergency room, was getting into the zone.
After experiencing the flood in Brazil and the mudflow in Bazhaixiang, Ling Ran was very used to handling such calamities, to begin with.
If there was something that he was not used to, it would be the fact that problems would always arise in terms of cooperation with other doctors.

Not only were the chief physicians and associate chief physicians who were leaders of treatment groups not used to Ling Ran’s leadership style, but attending physicians like Zhao Leyi were also not very willing to take orders from Ling Ran.
When faced with this situation, Ling Ran solved the problem by... doing it himself.
He did not even put the fact that there would be doctors who were unwilling to take orders from him into consideration.
It was just like how the doctors in the Emergency Medical Center never expected Ling Ran to possess such a great number of skills.
When it came to general surgeries, Ling Ran could deal with anything between the stomach and the an*s.
As for orthopedics surgeries, he could handle anything from the fingers to the elbow and from the toes to the knee.
He also knew all kinds of skills that could help a patient retain his or her life.
It could be said that Ling Ran was a lot more adept at treating patients with those ailments compared to other doctors.
As for patients who were not within that scope, ordinary emergency medical specialists were not capable of dealing with them either.
Ling Ran treated patients from one end of the emergency room to the other.
He then repeated the process.
Those who were willing to take orders from Ling Ran did things according to Ling Ran’s arrangements, while those who refused to do so naturally had their position as chief surgeon snatched away.
Even the only chief physician present, Chief Physician Tao, listened to Ling Ran’s orders.
He followed a patient on a gurney into an operating theater and did not emerge after that.
“Wow, is he Superman?” Zuo Cidian had just returned from the inpatient building, and he saw Ling Ran treating patients one by one at lightning speed.
As the doctor who was the best at administration in Yun Hua Emergency Medical Center, Zuo Cidian naturally did not think that what Ling Ran was doing was the best choice.
However, it was an extremely pleasing sight.
“Ling Ran truly lives up to his reputation of being skillful.” Dean Wu did not leave the emergency room.
He was standing beside Wang Chuangwen and peering at Ling Ran from afar with a look of admiration on his face.
“He’s blessed by God indeed.”
Zuo Cidian chuckled a few times and tried to downplay Ling Ran’s achievements so that he could make Ling Ran sound humble.
“That’s what Doctor Ling is like.
He doesn’t mind offending people if he has set his mind to something.”

“With such skills, he doesn’t need to worry about offending anyone in the Emergency Department.” Dean Wu laughed and said half-jokingly, “If it weren’t for the fact that Old Huo is too fierce, I would have asked Ling Ran to head to Yun Hua University and offend people.”
“Never say this in front of Department Director Huo.” Zuo Cidian’s shoulders tensed up a little without him realizing.
When he saw Wang Chuanwen, who was standing beside Dean Wu, he decided to put his social skills to use.
“You told me earlier that your three younger brothers will be here soon, right?
I’m afraid that Doctor Ling might be too busy to attend to them.
If you need stuff such as information, you can ask me about it.”
“There’s no rush.
As for you, is there any way that I can be of help?” Wang Chuanwen also put his great social skills to use.
Zuo Cidian froze for a moment.
“What do you mean by that?”
“We plan to make some donations and start a few charity projects in Changxi Province.
You guys...
I mean, what does Doctor Ling need the most right now?” Wang Chuanwen’s gaze followed Ling Ran’s blue scrubs.
Most of the doctors in the emergency room were clad in large white coats, and Ling Ran’s blue scrubs were especially jarring amid the sea of large white coats.
In addition, Wang Chuanwen was giving his silent approval to Ling Ran’s efficiency and style of getting things done.

chapters.title: Chapter 897: Top Skills
paragraphs: “What is it that we need the most right now?” Zuo Cidian repeated what Wang Chuanwen said while his mind worked at high speed.

He looked at Dean Wu out of the corner of his eyes. As the dean of Yun Hua University School of Medicine, Dean Wu Junior inherited his father’s career and had a lot of connections, so he had a more accurate judgment toward the current situation than most people.

At this time, Dean Wu broke into a faint smile. He did not seem worried about the possibility of the donation for Yun Hua University School of Medicine being split between the university and the hospital just because of that.
Perhaps they had already come up with an agreement for the donation?
Or did the Wang family have more funds that giving out one more donation would not affect others?

Zuo Cidian thought of many things in an instant, but from others’ perspectives, he had just thought for a moment. Then, Zuo Cidian made his decision and said, “Recently, Doctor Ling has always wanted an ICU for himself. What I mean is that he wants an ICU that belongs to the Emergency Department.”

The younger brother, Wang Chuanli, was staying at the ICU, so Wang Chuanwen had seen that facilities and equipment inside before. He said, “Is the ICU in Yun Hua Hospital not good or convenient enough?”

Zuo Cidian immediately answered, “It’s mainly not convenient enough, and the hospital beds are always not enough. Doctor Ling often performs major surgeries, so after the surgery, the patient will be transferred to the ICU, and there are risks. Besides, Doctor Ling’s surgical volume is very big, just like what you’ve seen, he always performs surgery during dawn. Now, he is forced to stop performing surgeries because of insufficient hospital beds in the ICU.”
Wang Chuanwen slowly nodded.

“The ICU that the Emergency Department has planned for ourselves isn’t very big. It can just be located at the podium at the west, and five to six hospital beds will be very good.” Zuo Cidian smiled faintly before he spoke again, “The hospital has agreed with this a long while ago, but the management could not bring out the funds, so they are not quite willing to approve of the funds for this either.”

“Let me gain some understanding of the situation first.” Wang Chuanwen did not immediately make his decision. He did not even ask Zuo Cidian how much money was needed. After all, he could easily figure out these matters later.

“I should get busy, then. Dean Wu, Mister Wang, pardon me.” Zuo Cidian nodded. He did not hang around the area. It was not as if Wang Chuanwen could come to a decision if Zuo Cidian just hung around. Of course, his face was not something someone would want to see hanging around the area.

“Dean Wu, you should leave if you’re busy, I want to take a look for a little while longer.” Wang Chuanwen did not have anything to do. At this time, he stared at Ling Ran walk from a cubicle to another cubicle like a tank storming fortifications, so he did not want to leave at the moment.
Dean Wu smiled and said, “I’ll also watch with you for a while. It’s been some time since I saw such a busy emergency room.”

“Alright.” Wang Chuanwen did not make a pretense of trying to send Dean Wu away either. He still stared straight ahead, and he opened up a topic of conversation. “Is Doctor Ling helping out other doctors?”
Dean Wu almost laughed. He coughed and said, “Doctor Ling is... solving problems.”
“He’s a doctor who solves problems?” Wang Chuanwen nodded slightly. “Doctors who can solve problems are good doctors.”
“You’re right,” Dean Wu agreed.
From the professional Dean Wu’s perspective, Ling Ran was currently the equivalent of a heavy tank. His moving speed was very slow, but his attack speed and frequency of attack were even slower.

However, whenever Ling Ran entered a cubicle, the young doctors inside would show a look of fear, helplessness, or just sigh. They were just like a lone wolf who attacked an antelope fiercely but was knocked around until its head was swollen. Then, it noticed in fear that a gigantic lion walked over and sent the antelope sprawling on the ground with just one paw.
Although the wolf still had some leftover meat to eat, its efforts from fighting hard eventually became food the lion handed to it in contempt, and this feeling was indeed very... addicting.

The young doctors were unhappy, resigned, and slightly angry, but after Ling Ran worked for one, two, and three rounds, they got used to the feeling of having a lion at their backs, while the feeling of their food being snatched had slowly developed into the feeling of them relying on Ling Ran.

After adapting to the rhythm, the young doctors even automatically finished the preoperation, so when Ling Ran entered, he could complete the main task at a super fast speed with the standard maneuvers... Right then, the wolves became jackals. They turned into creatures that feasted on fresh meat to creatures that feasted on carrion.
“Does Doctor Ling’s skills obviously surpass his peers’?” Even if Wang Chuanwen did not understand what was going on, he could know the general gist through observing other people.

From the facial expressions of different doctors, Wang Chuanwen saw resignation, enlightenment, admiration, and relief. Similarly, he saw anger, lamentation, and self-reproach. The only thing he did not see was a competitive spirit.
Wang Chuanwen saw this kind of emotional change multiple times in his own factory, and that was usually when the general workers faced the amazing technicians.
He did not expect he would see such a condition in the hospital, and that he would see it so many times with so many variations.
Dean Wu chuckled and said, “He has definitely surpassed his peers.”
“Oh yes, is Doctor Ling a doctor who can perform surgery independently?” Wang Chuanwen asked deliberately.

“The group leaders of treatment groups are generally made up of chief physicians and associate chief physicians in a hospital like Yun Hua Hospital. Only when it’s a very special situation, attending physicians can occasionally hold the position.” Dean Wu was also willing to boast about Ling Ran a little. Ling Ran had successfully completed the surgery for Dean Wu Senior, and the prognosis was perfect. For a professional like Dean Wu, not only did his family receive the best medical service, but he also experienced Ling Ran’s superb operation and control during the perioperative period throughout his father’s entire treatment. In any hospital and country, this kind of doctor was worthy of praise.
Wang Chuanwen nodded. “So, Doctor Ling can manage operations on his own now.”

“He can also act as the leader of his team.” Dean Wu looked at where Ling Ran currently stood, directing Wang Chuanwen to look at Ling Ran along the direction of his eyes, he said, “Although he operates differently from the medical management mode that I expected him to be on, you can’t say that this medical management mode isn’t good, considering the fact that he has such abilities and is able to use it in such a manner.”
Certain figures instantly popped up in Wang Chuanwen’s mind, so he could not help but nod and say, “Relying on one’s skills when leading a team is the most common sight in the machinery industry.”

“Is it? Actually, it’s about the same for the hospital, but it isn’t very obvious. Some hospital managements are resourceful. They rely on the relationships and profits to fool the doctors into working. Some of the hospital managers are veterans in the field, and they rely on their disciples to support them. Some are like Ling Ran, who have top-class skills and can naturally rely on their skills to lead their teams and become outstanding by just quietly working.”
Wang Chuanwen listened and nodded quietly while he thought about the “top-class skills” that Dean Wu mentioned.
Wang Chuanwen’s other three siblings arrived at Yun Hua Hospital, and when they entered, they saw that the hospital while it was at its busiest moment.

The second and third batches of burn patients had been sent in. The number of burn victims had been reduced, but now, the number of patients sent into the hospital due to smoke inhalation injuries had increased. Five to six people were seen holding buckets and vomiting blood at the same time, which made the scene strangely shocking.
“Where’s our third brother? How is he?” The three siblings met up at the airport. At this time, they found Wang Chuanwen, and their agitation slowly faded away.
“In the ICU. Wait a minute, I’ll look for a doctor and tell him.” As Wang Chuanwen said that, he waved at Zuo Cidian, who had just run over.
“The doctors look so busy.”
“It’s okay, this doctor doesn’t give consultation.” Once Wang Chuanwen said that, he shouted, “Doctor Zuo, Doctor Zuo...”

chapters.title: Chapter 898: Heart
paragraphs: Zuo Cidian walked over with a smile on his face.

He was not actually considered bigger. A report on the fire had already come out, and other departments with vacant beds had already helped out by taking in patients. They had also cleared out all the regular patients in the emergency room that they could.
1As for the patients who had just arrived, various departments were willing to take in those who were eligible to be transferred. Departments needed patients to operate, after all.
As for patients who were not eligible for transfer, they treated those who could be treated on the spot and turned away those who could not be treated on the spot.

Hence, compared to how busy a doctor usually was, Zuo Cidian was feeling very relaxed right now. Even though it was a little annoying to pass messages around, it was, after all, a less stressful affair. Zuo Cidian was even a little happy to see that Wang Chuanwen and Dean Wu were still in the emergency room.
This meant that they had the intention to donate for real. If they did not, forget about Wang Chuanwen who had a lot of time on his hands, Dean Wu definitely would not stay here until now.
When Zuo Cidian thought about how Ling Ran would have his personal ICU... no, when he thought about how the Emergency Medical Center would have its own ICU, he could not help but smile.
“Zuo Cidian, these are the three brothers of mine.” Wang Chuanwen moved aside and gestured at his three brothers. He then said, “Doctor Zuo, can you arrange for us to visit our third brother today?”

“No problem.” Zuo Cidian was an intelligent man, and he first agreed to the request. He then said to Wang Chuanwen’s three brothers, who were standing behind Wang Chuanwen. “A building had caught fire today, and many burn patients had been sent over. The people in the ICU are probably super busy now. Please wait for a whole, and I’ll ask an intern to see how the situation there is. If it’s convenient for them, we’ll go up there.”

The three brothers had seen how tense the atmosphere in the emergency room was. Wang Chuanwen’s second brother who was standing beside him said, “It’s okay. Since our third brother’s condition is stable, it doesn’t matter whether we visit him sooner or later.”

Zuo Cidian breathed a sigh of relief when he saw that the other party was an amiable person. As they may make a donation, he took the initiative to get close to the Wang brothers. “Thank you for understanding. Actually, since Doctor Ling personally operated on Mr. Wang Chuanli, and the surgery went really well, you guys don’t have to worry too much... Hm, are you Mister Wang Chuanli’s older or younger brother?”
“I’m the second oldest in the family.”
Zuo Cidian hummed in acknowledgment, “Then, does it mean that you are Mister Wang Chuanwu?”
The expressions of the four Wang brothers who were standing in front of Zuo Cidian changed a little.
“Mister Zuo, you’re pretty imaginative.” The second Wang brother scratched his head and forced a smile.

Someone else would think that the second Wang brother was not able to flash a sincere smile because his brother was injured and he was not in a good mood. But Zuo Cidian was a clever man, and he realized that he might have made the wrong guess.

He did not mind that he had made a wrong guess as he was just trying to get close to the Wang brothers, anyway. He merely smiled and said, “You know, the older generation likes to talk about ‘ren’ (benevolence), ‘yi’ (righteousness), ‘li’ (etiquette), ‘zhi’ (wisdom) and ‘xin’ (belief). And you know how they always talk about how a man must be adept at both ‘wen’ (studies) and ‘wu’ (martial arts)? Among my extended relatives, quite a lot named their children in the order of ‘wen’, ‘wu’, ‘li’, ‘zhu’, and ‘xin’...”

“When I was born, I was so intelligent that I could beat Confucius.” The oldest in the family, Wang Chuanwen coughed a few times and said, “We are named in the order of ‘wen’ (wisdom), ‘ming’ (enlightenment), ‘li’ (etiquette), and ‘mao'(politeness).”
Zuo Cidian froze for a moment. That only totaled up to four names, right?

Zuo Cidian’s gaze floated past the oldest brother, Wang Chuanwen; the second brother, Wang Chuanming; and the fourth brother, Wang Chuanmao. His gaze fell upon the fifth and youngest brother, and he suddenly had a realization. ‘This man was an accident, wasn’t he? His parents didn’t even prepare a name for him!’
The fifth brother was rather young, and he had a fair complexion. He saw Zuo Cidian looking at him and said, “My name is Wang Chuanfu .”
The oldest brother, Wang Chuanwen whispered, “When our fifth brother was born, the economic reform had happened.”
When it was time for everyone to get off work, the hustle and bustle in the Emergency Medical Center had already died down.
Yun Hua Hospital had taken in more than twenty burn patients, and Huo Congjun’s treatment group had to work overtime for many hours. They also took half the manpower of other treatment groups.

A person could not expect burn patients to be taken care of by their family members. Not only that but burn patients who were kept under observation in the hospital had to be observed at all times. This was ten times more arduous for the medical staff members compared to taking care of ordinary patients.
Lu Wenbin and two housemen were called to help out in the Burn Center.

But because of how Ling Ran had worked at lightning speed, the number of patients in the emergency room had reduced greatly. Now, aside from some patients who required observation, most of the patients in the emergency room were those who fell under the scope of internal medicine.

This was when Zuo Cidian reported to Ling Ran. “The doctors in the ICU are slightly less busy now, and I am about to bring the four Wang brothers there to visit their brother. We should keep them happy, as they might just build an ICU for us. That would be great.”
Ling Ran did not really care about the first half of the sentence, but he could not help but get excited at the possibility of having his own ICU.

Even if a person were to disregard how complicated it was to run an ICU and how necessary an ICU was, if he were able to get an ICU with five beds inside, it would mean that he had five extra hospital beds at his disposal. If the ICU comprised of ten beds, it would mean that he had so many extra hospital beds that they could create three rooms in one ward!

The longer a doctor had worked in a hospital, the more he would care about the number of hospital beds. This was especially true in top tertiary Grade A hospitals like Yun Hua Hospital. It was not an understatement to say that it was hard to even find a vacant bed in the hospital. Some departments would even delegate the hospital beds to their associate chief physicians or even chief physicians, and this brought about a lot of competition.
“Let’s head there together. I can do my ward rounds while I’m at it,” Ling Ran decided.
Having his own ICU was an extremely important matter, and he did not mind making a trip to the ICU for it.
Zuo Cidian did not find it strange. He was not surprised either. He walked over to talk to the four Wang brothers about this. They then gathered and walked toward the ICU.
At this moment, the ICU was already full of patients.
The doctors and nurses were basically floating as they hurried around to administer all kinds of treatment while the patients who were suffering from various ailments lay in bed.

The four Wang brothers looked into ICU through the glass window and saw that both Wang Chuanli’s hands and legs were bound. They had no idea whether he was conscious or not, and they became so anxious that they were like ants on a hot pan as they stood outside the ICU.

“The visiting hours every day are fixed, and you guys can go in one by one to see him. But due to how busy the doctors are today, you can only stand here and look at him,” Zuo Cidian explained things to the Wang brothers in a whisper and stood aside.
Ling Ran stood aside too. Not only could he see the situation in the ICU, but he was also not blocking the Wang brothers’ view.
*Beep... Beep...*
The monitor in the ICU was letting out monotonous beeps, and they rang out through the glass door. The beeps were making the Wang brothers agitated.
“Big brother, how can this not be considered serious?” The fourth brother, Wang Chuanmao felt extremely uncomfortable when he saw his shirtless brother being tied up in bed all naked like that.
This was not the first time Wang Chuanwen had seen this. He said in a deep and profound tone, “He’s a lot better than how he used to be. Isn’t continuous recovery good enough?”
As if to authenticate what Wang Chuanwen had just said, the moment he finished speaking, one of the monitors in the ICU let out loud and violent beeps.
To the medical staff members in the ICU, this kind of beeps was a call to action.
A doctor hurried over in a few seconds. He took off his stethoscope as he said, “His BP and heart rate have fallen. Epinephrine, quick!”
As the doctor spoke, he started performing chest compressions.
To doctors working in the ICU, CPR was something they had to do almost every day. Even though the medical staff members were nervous, it was not to the point that the ICU descended into chaos.
“Octreotide...
“Continue administering epinephrine...

“Dopamine!” The doctor barked orders nonstop at his subordinate, and he did not stop performing chest compressions at the same time. But the line on the heart rate monitor was still as flat as an airplane runway.
As the four Wang brothers stood outside the ICU and looked at the scene, they were suddenly a little worried and terrified. But at the same time, they were also relieved.
At least, the loud and violent beeps were not ringing out of their third brother’s monitor.
“You can increase the dosage of the epinephrine.” Ling Ran grabbed the phone by the window and said.
When the young nurse who answered the call heard Ling Ran’s voice, she passed Ling Ran’s message without hesitation.
The attending physician in the ICU hesitated for a moment, but he decided to do as Ling Ran said.

This time, the heart rate monitor let out a beep, and the patient regained his sinus rhythm.
The attending physician in the ICU could not help but look at Ling Ran and flashed a relatively friendly smile.
The patient was successfully resuscitated, and he did not really care about who took credit for it. What mattered the most was that it was a happy ending.
Ling Ran responded with a socially appropriate smile.
He possessed Perfect Level CPR, and this skill could really be put into good use when resuscitating patients in the CPR.
The four Wang brothers let out a sigh of relief. Their expressions had changed when they looked at Ling Ran again.
However, at this moment, Ling Ran furrowed his eyebrows a little.
A new mission from the system had appeared before his eyes.

[Mission Reward: Cardiac Trauma Repair (Master Level)]

sentences.text: Zuo Cidian walked over with a smile on his face.
He was not actually considered bigger.
A report on the fire had already come out, and other departments with vacant beds had already helped out by taking in patients.
They had also cleared out all the regular patients in the emergency room that they could.
1As for the patients who had just arrived, various departments were willing to take in those who were eligible to be transferred.
Departments needed patients to operate, after all.
As for patients who were not eligible for transfer, they treated those who could be treated on the spot and turned away those who could not be treated on the spot.
Hence, compared to how busy a doctor usually was, Zuo Cidian was feeling very relaxed right now.
Even though it was a little annoying to pass messages around, it was, after all, a less stressful affair.
Zuo Cidian was even a little happy to see that Wang Chuanwen and Dean Wu were still in the emergency room.
This meant that they had the intention to donate for real.
If they did not, forget about Wang Chuanwen who had a lot of time on his hands, Dean Wu definitely would not stay here until now.
When Zuo Cidian thought about how Ling Ran would have his personal ICU... no, when he thought about how the Emergency Medical Center would have its own ICU, he could not help but smile.
“Zuo Cidian, these are the three brothers of mine.” Wang Chuanwen moved aside and gestured at his three brothers.
He then said, “Doctor Zuo, can you arrange for us to visit our third brother today?”
“No problem.” Zuo Cidian was an intelligent man, and he first agreed to the request.
He then said to Wang Chuanwen’s three brothers, who were standing behind Wang Chuanwen.
“A building had caught fire today, and many burn patients had been sent over.
The people in the ICU are probably super busy now.
Please wait for a whole, and I’ll ask an intern to see how the situation there is.
If it’s convenient for them, we’ll go up there.”
The three brothers had seen how tense the atmosphere in the emergency room was.
Wang Chuanwen’s second brother who was standing beside him said, “It’s okay.
Since our third brother’s condition is stable, it doesn’t matter whether we visit him sooner or later.”
Zuo Cidian breathed a sigh of relief when he saw that the other party was an amiable person.
As they may make a donation, he took the initiative to get close to the Wang brothers.
“Thank you for understanding.
Actually, since Doctor Ling personally operated on Mr.
Wang Chuanli, and the surgery went really well, you guys don’t have to worry too much...
Hm, are you Mister Wang Chuanli’s older or younger brother?”
“I’m the second oldest in the family.”
Zuo Cidian hummed in acknowledgment, “Then, does it mean that you are Mister Wang Chuanwu?”
The expressions of the four Wang brothers who were standing in front of Zuo Cidian changed a little.
“Mister Zuo, you’re pretty imaginative.” The second Wang brother scratched his head and forced a smile.
Someone else would think that the second Wang brother was not able to flash a sincere smile because his brother was injured and he was not in a good mood.
But Zuo Cidian was a clever man, and he realized that he might have made the wrong guess.
He did not mind that he had made a wrong guess as he was just trying to get close to the Wang brothers, anyway.
He merely smiled and said, “You know, the older generation likes to talk about ‘ren’ (benevolence), ‘yi’ (righteousness), ‘li’ (etiquette), ‘zhi’ (wisdom) and ‘xin’ (belief).
And you know how they always talk about how a man must be adept at both ‘wen’ (studies) and ‘wu’ (martial arts)?
Among my extended relatives, quite a lot named their children in the order of ‘wen’, ‘wu’, ‘li’, ‘zhu’, and ‘xin’...”

“When I was born, I was so intelligent that I could beat Confucius.” The oldest in the family, Wang Chuanwen coughed a few times and said, “We are named in the order of ‘wen’ (wisdom), ‘ming’ (enlightenment), ‘li’ (etiquette), and ‘mao'(politeness).”
Zuo Cidian froze for a moment.
That only totaled up to four names, right?
Zuo Cidian’s gaze floated past the oldest brother, Wang Chuanwen; the second brother, Wang Chuanming; and the fourth brother, Wang Chuanmao.
His gaze fell upon the fifth and youngest brother, and he suddenly had a realization.
‘This man was an accident, wasn’t he?
His parents didn’t even prepare a name for him!’
The fifth brother was rather young, and he had a fair complexion.
He saw Zuo Cidian looking at him and said, “My name is Wang Chuanfu .”
The oldest brother, Wang Chuanwen whispered, “When our fifth brother was born, the economic reform had happened.”
When it was time for everyone to get off work, the hustle and bustle in the Emergency Medical Center had already died down.
Yun Hua Hospital had taken in more than twenty burn patients, and Huo Congjun’s treatment group had to work overtime for many hours.
They also took half the manpower of other treatment groups.
A person could not expect burn patients to be taken care of by their family members.
Not only that but burn patients who were kept under observation in the hospital had to be observed at all times.
This was ten times more arduous for the medical staff members compared to taking care of ordinary patients.
Lu Wenbin and two housemen were called to help out in the Burn Center.
But because of how Ling Ran had worked at lightning speed, the number of patients in the emergency room had reduced greatly.
Now, aside from some patients who required observation, most of the patients in the emergency room were those who fell under the scope of internal medicine.
This was when Zuo Cidian reported to Ling Ran.
“The doctors in the ICU are slightly less busy now, and I am about to bring the four Wang brothers there to visit their brother.
We should keep them happy, as they might just build an ICU for us.
That would be great.”
Ling Ran did not really care about the first half of the sentence, but he could not help but get excited at the possibility of having his own ICU.

Even if a person were to disregard how complicated it was to run an ICU and how necessary an ICU was, if he were able to get an ICU with five beds inside, it would mean that he had five extra hospital beds at his disposal.
If the ICU comprised of ten beds, it would mean that he had so many extra hospital beds that they could create three rooms in one ward!
The longer a doctor had worked in a hospital, the more he would care about the number of hospital beds.
This was especially true in top tertiary Grade A hospitals like Yun Hua Hospital.
It was not an understatement to say that it was hard to even find a vacant bed in the hospital.
Some departments would even delegate the hospital beds to their associate chief physicians or even chief physicians, and this brought about a lot of competition.
“Let’s head there together.
I can do my ward rounds while I’m at it,” Ling Ran decided.
Having his own ICU was an extremely important matter, and he did not mind making a trip to the ICU for it.
Zuo Cidian did not find it strange.
He was not surprised either.
He walked over to talk to the four Wang brothers about this.
They then gathered and walked toward the ICU.
At this moment, the ICU was already full of patients.
The doctors and nurses were basically floating as they hurried around to administer all kinds of treatment while the patients who were suffering from various ailments lay in bed.
The four Wang brothers looked into ICU through the glass window and saw that both Wang Chuanli’s hands and legs were bound.
They had no idea whether he was conscious or not, and they became so anxious that they were like ants on a hot pan as they stood outside the ICU.
“The visiting hours every day are fixed, and you guys can go in one by one to see him.
But due to how busy the doctors are today, you can only stand here and look at him,” Zuo Cidian explained things to the Wang brothers in a whisper and stood aside.
Ling Ran stood aside too.
Not only could he see the situation in the ICU, but he was also not blocking the Wang brothers’ view.
*Beep...
Beep...*
The monitor in the ICU was letting out monotonous beeps, and they rang out through the glass door.
The beeps were making the Wang brothers agitated.
“Big brother, how can this not be considered serious?” The fourth brother, Wang Chuanmao felt extremely uncomfortable when he saw his shirtless brother being tied up in bed all naked like that.
This was not the first time Wang Chuanwen had seen this.
He said in a deep and profound tone, “He’s a lot better than how he used to be.
Isn’t continuous recovery good enough?”

Even though the medical staff members were nervous, it was not to the point that the ICU descended into chaos.
“Octreotide...

But the line on the heart rate monitor was still as flat as an airplane runway.
As the four Wang brothers stood outside the ICU and looked at the scene, they were suddenly a little worried and terrified.

chapters.title: Chapter 899: I Want to Go In
paragraphs: Ling Ran read the mission seriously one more time.
Doctors had heard a lot of cardiac trauma repair, yet they rarely encountered it.

They seldom saw it because patients with penetrating cardiac injury were relatively rare, but they heard it many times before because cardiac trauma repair had opened the path for people to explore the field of cardiovascular surgery so that people in the medical field were familiar with it.
In the past, the father of surgery, Theodor Billroth said something that was a classic. “Anyone who attempts heart surgery will fall into disrepute.”
This sentence had a far-reaching influence since he was the authority in the field of surgery in the past. So, for a long time, no medical student tried to touch the heart again.
It was only three years after Billroth’s death that Louis Appia, a Frankfurt doctor, successfully performed a cardiac trauma repair.

It was hard to say whether Doctor Appia was ready and was waiting for the opportunity to perform this surgery or whether he was just a pure genius with great luck, so much so that the first time he ran into a rare patient with a heart injury for the first time, he actually successfully performed cardiac trauma repair on him.
At any generation, cardiac surgery was extremely difficult, and it was practically a quagmire.
In 1896, though, on the twenty-second year of Emperor Guangxu’s rule over China, when surgeons performed cardiac surgeries, their scalpels also moved with much greater precision and confidence.

During that time, there was no cardiopulmonary bypass, and of course, for many years after that, there was no cardiopulmonary bypass either. At that time, this technique had not been refined just yet, and it was not great, but what was great was that during the nineteenth century, there were practically no blood transfusion techniques available. This meant that when a surgeon performed a heart surgery, it would be an extremely high-end surgery where the heart would beat nonstop right when the surgeon performed open-heart surgery, and the surgeon could not even think about getting any blood transfusion.
In terms of risks, there were not many medical surgeries that were more dangerous than this.

From another point of view, however, being able to complete cardiac trauma repairs using such an outdated surgery technique in such a dangerous environment meant that the technique was not actually that hard.
In fact, if anyone just listened to the description of the surgery, it was actually very easy.

Doctor Appia’s original words were: I decided to open the chest through the fourth intercostal space on the left... enlarge the pericardial rupture, expose the heart, remove the blood and blood clots. I then found a 0.6 inches rupture on the surface of the right ventricle. Next, I pressed on the rupture with my fingers to stop the bleeding. I used a fine intestinal needle and silk thread to perform a knot during diastole. When the third suture was completed, the amount of bleeding was obviously reduced and was under control...’

In other words, there were two most important surgery steps for Doctor Appia. The first step was to stop bleeding with his hands and control the cardiac rupture. The second step was to quickly do a triple suture on the heart before it even figured out what was happening.
This was the first successful heart surgery in human history.
Up to now, there was no doubt that the conditions for the surgery had been upgraded, and the steps of the surgery had also changed. But the main steps had not changed much.
The surgeon had to locate the rupture at the heart, push it down to control it, and when the heart was beating at the slowest, suture the rupture.
If Ling Ran were given a chance, he might be able to complete such a cardiac trauma repair independently with his current skills.
However, if and only if there was no suitable opportunity, even in the current medical environment, Ling Ran would not want to touch a heart at all.
Without enough accumulation of experience, Ling Ran would not want to touch a heart recklessly.

Doctor Appia, who was the first person to complete a cardiac surgery in human history, operated on one hundred and twenty-three patients who required cardiac trauma repair, and the mortality rate was at sixty percent. Therefore, the risk of experimental surgery was huge.
However, the skill was given by the system, and he would not have to worry so much about experimenting.
Therefore, he should place great emphasis on completing this quest.
Ling Ran closed his eyes and pondered about it before he opened his eyes and looked into the ICU. Then, he began to think about how to go in and help.

Although the Intensive Care Department was a small department, it was a complete department. When people from other departments came in to help, that person might seem as if he did not have a legitimate reason to help at all...
There was only one Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery and He Yuanzheng. It was not easy to find another easy, friendly, gentle, and kind department and department director.
“Zuo Cidian.” Ling Ran decided to give the problem to someone else. “What can I do to help the patient in the ICU?”

“Huh?” Zuo Cidian was prepared to flatter the Wang siblings. After he heard Ling Ran’s question, he decided to serve Ling Ran instead. “Doctor Ling, even though the ICU is busy, they do have enough manpower inside. Let’s not go in and help.”

The ICU was not similar to the Emergency Department. It did not have periods of time where it had the most patients or least patients. For hospitals like Yun Hua Hospital, the ICU was basically always at max capacity. There would always only be three beds left out of the twenty beds they had. The three empty beds did not mean that there were no patients for them, but they were kept empty for maneuvering purposes so that they could avoid losing their composure when they had to handle emergencies.
The ICU was just as busy today, but it was only because it was just full of patients. When the doctors in the ICU came together to work, they would still be able to take care of them.
Ling Ran looked inside and said in a very determined tone, “I’m going in to help.”
“Fine... whatever you say.” That was all Zuo Cidian could say. Ling Ran’s skills were really great, but his personality...

Zuo Cidian gritted his teeth. What was there to be picky about surgeons’ attitudes? Compared with other surgeons who were perverted, arrogant, egotistical, had low self-esteem, had manic issues, and had anger issues, Ling Ran’s personality was so much better.

“Let’s go into the ICU in the name of making a ward round.” After Zuo Cidian thought long and hard about it, he whispered, “Let’s present our ward round as a fait accompli first. You’ll go in for the ward rounds first, and when you encounter critically ill patients... Well, if you go in for about twenty minutes or half an hour at most, you’ll have a great chance of meeting critically-ill patients. Then, you can participate in the surgery. Once everyone starts to get busy, they won’t care about you anymore. If you are lucky, you might rescue one or two patients.”
“One or two is too few,” Ling Ran said.

“Just help in resuscitating the patients first. I’ve taken a look, there are still many patients in the ICU today, and the severity of their illnesses is high as well. Just linger around for a while, and you might be able to join the rescue.” Zuo Cidian could only spontaneously think of a normal lousy idea that was not really a lousy idea.
Ling Ran nodded in agreement. This plan was not so complicated.

Zuo Cidian sighed as he watched Ling Ran wash his hands. He took out his phone and prepared to dial the number of an attending physician he was familiar with. Ling Ran’s treatment group often came to the ICU for their ward rounds. The first step of the plan was certainly not a problem.

Wang Chuanwen looked at Zuo Cidian and sighed. He could not help but come to a misunderstanding and said, “Doctor Zuo, Doctor Ling doesn’t actually need to show us his skills or anything. No matter how his performance is, it doesn’t affect our decision whether we will donate or not.”
“Huh? Oh, it’s nothing...” Zuo Cidian was stunned for a while before he registered what he meant. Wang Chuanwen thought that Ling Ran wanted to go to the ICU to show off.
But even though Zuo Cidian did not think so, he could not stop the Wang brothers from thinking that way. But even if they thought of it that way, it did not matter.
Zuo Cidian made another call again with a perfunctory tone, saying that Ling Ran wanted to go for his ward rounds and so on...
A few moments later, Ling Ran came in with his hands held over his chest.
“Doctor Ling, you may enter after you get dressed,” Zuo Cidian told Ling Ran.
Ling Ran nodded then looked at the Wang siblings.
All four of the Wang siblings looked up and smiled in approval.
Ling Ran said in puzzlement, “Why are they still here? You can send them away now.”
The Wang siblings could not help but feel shocked.
Zuo Cidian then understood what Ling Ran was thinking. He quickly smiled at Wang Chuanwen and the others. “I’m sorry, let’s head back first. Visiting hours are actually over.”
All four of the Wang siblings were led back to the elevator with dazed looks on their faces. They felt that something was wrong.

chapters.title: Chapter 900: Boring
paragraphs: “I’m here to... carry out my ward rounds.” As Ling Ran walked into the ICU, his spirits were up, and he almost blurted out that he was there to help.

The nurses in the ICU were very excited too, and they did not notice this tiny detail at all. One of them stood beside Ling Ran and reported, “We have been paying attention to all the patients you sent over, Doctor Ling. Right now, the only one who’s in an unstable condition is the patient in Bed 2, and his heart has failed twice. The patient in Bed 4 didn’t really urinate much today... The others are doing pretty fine...”
The most common sight in the ICU was the gradual revival of patients who had previously been given their death sentences. Of course, it was also common for patients to die all of a sudden.

Compared with the patients whom other doctors sent over who were suffering from major ailments such as serious myocardial or cerebral infarction, organ failure or even unknown illnesses, the patients whom Ling Ran sent over to the ICU usually recovered better. This was especially true for patients who underwent scheduled surgery. They usually only stayed for a short while in the ICU, and it was mostly for precautionary purposes. This was also why Ling Ran enjoyed such a good reputation in the hospital.
If a person wanted to know who was the most skillful doctor in a hospital, the nurses would be able to give him the best answer.
Only the nurses in the ICU knew which doctor was the one who was the most meticulous with the scalpel.
Ling Ran flashed a socially appropriate smile. He then surveyed his patients one by one.

For some time, he had been frequently making ward rounds in the ICU. This was the most the doctors in the ICU allowed him to do. They were not as easy to bully as the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery.
Zuo Cidian was not allowed to follow Ling Ran. He saw the four Wang brothers off before he went back to where he was standing and observed things through the glass window.

The patients whose conditions were the most critical in the hospital were gathered in the ICU, and this was why doctors had to make frequent ward rounds in the ICU. Most patients there were unable to speak, and even those who were conscious would need to use up every ounce of energy in their bodies to answer a yes or no question.

Because of this, there was not much that doctors could do during ward rounds. Most of the time, when doctors made ward rounds in the ICU, they would be reading examination reports and looking at all kinds of data. Tests such as blood and sputum culture would be done on conventional patients in the ICU, and they would sometimes require a CT scan, an ultrasound scan or a series of biochemical tests. For each patient, there would be so many authorization forms for examinations that they could make up a book.
Ling Ran deliberately slowed down as he flipped through the examination reports.

He had long since been interested in cardiac surgery. Truth be told, every medical student would dream about carrying out cardiac surgery the moment they step into the hospital. However, for some of them, this dream would be shattered the moment they graduated or were assigned to a certain department. For the rest of them, this dream would only be shattered after they enter the Cardiovascular Surgery Department.
The Cardiovascular Surgery Department was never friendly to newcomers.

Not only was this because cardiac surgery was difficult, but it was also because competition within the Cardiovascular Surgery Department was strong. In every Cardiovascular Surgery Department that was good enough, there would be several, or even more than ten skilled surgeons who could operate on patients.
Cardiac trauma repair, which the system was offering to Ling Ran as a reward if he were to complete the mission, was a good starting point.
Ling Ran looked around. He then read the report he was holding silently. Like usual, he slowly got into the kind of zone doctors were in when they made ward rounds.
A nurse followed Ling Ran and helped him out with a smile on her face.
Zuo Cidian, who was watching the scene while standing in front of the glass window, felt envious.
The nurses in the ICU were famous for being fierce, and such a smile was hard to come by.
“It seems like none of the patients are in danger.” Wang Chuanwen’s voice rang out from behind Zuo Cidian.
Zuo Cidian was a little shocked, but he was not shameless enough to be angry at Wang Chuanwen over this. “Why are you back?”
“It’s boring down there,” Wang Chuanwen gave a simple explanation.
He was no longer a youth who would admit to anything other people called him out over. He was only willing to explain his presence outside the ICU because the other party was a doctor.
Zuo Cidian turned and saw Wang Chuanming, Wang Chuanmao, and Wang Chuanfu. He realized that it was easy to recall their names when all of them were present...
“Doctor Zuo?” Wang Chuanwen nudged Zuo Cidian, who was kind of absentminded. “It seems that the situation inside isn’t going according to your speculation.”
Zuo Cidian nodded. He then whispered, “It’s very normal for patients in the ICU to be in danger. Things will not stay calm for long.”
After he said that, Zuo Cidian specifically added, “The condition of your younger brother is considered quite mild compared to the other patients in the ICU. So, you don’t need to be too worried.”

Wang Chuanwen shook his head and said, “You said that I don’t need to worry about my younger brother, but you also said that it’s very normal for patients in the ICU to be in danger. Which statement should I believe in?”

Zuo Cidian froze for a moment. He had no choice but to give an earnest explanation. “All the patients who are in the most critical conditions in the hospital are gathered in the ICU. For patients sent over from the Emergency Department such as your younger brother, things are different. Even though your younger brother was involved in a serious accident, he’s still relatively young and in good health. Moreover, Doctor Ling was the one who operated on him. This is why your younger brother’s condition is relatively stable...”
“As long as things are going fine, it’s good.” Wang Chuanwen did not continue to ask questions. He then glanced at the glass window and asked, “How long would we need to wait for?”

Zuo Cidian did not answer Wang Chuanwen’s question. The youngest Wang brother, Wang Chuanfu, who was standing behind Wang Chuanwen, flatly said, “There are so many doctors and nurses in the ICU, and I’m sure that it’s not for decorative purposes.”
“Hm.” Wang Chuanwen nodded. He did agree with it.
As they were thinking about this, one of the monitors near the door started beeping.
Ling Ran strode toward the bed and got there before anyone else.
“Doctor Ling?” The attending physician looked a little doubtfully at Ling Ran.
“I’m here to help,” Ling Ran explained.
If some random junior doctor were the one doing this, the attending physician would have definitely scolded him. But as this person was Ling Ran, the attending physician did not dare to offend him.
‘He’s a doctor from another department who encountered a patient who’s in danger in the ICU, and he wants to help out. Should I let him?’
There seemed to be no point in forcing Ling Ran not to help.
When the attending physician thought of this, he flashed an expression as if he was released of his burden.
Ling Ran slowly observed the attending physician’s changing expression.
From what he could remember, this change in expression had also happened to He Yuanzheng before... When Ling Ran noticed this, he found it pretty interesting.
“The right pupil is dilated, and the left pulse is weak...” The attending physician still had a right to bark orders, and he quickly reported his findings.
Ling Ran reached out in a natural manner and palpated the patient’s abdomen. The result was not a satisfactory one.

“Administer dopamine to maintain his blood pressure... Prepare for left chest drainage... Call a doctor from the Cardiothoracic Surgery Department over for a consultation...” After the attending physician barked his orders, he could not help but look diffidently at Ling Ran.
All the doctors in Yun Hua Hospital admitted defeat to Ling Ran when it came to skills.
Ling Ran nodded a little. “This will do.”

“Prepare for an abdominal ultrasound, electrocardiography, and arterial blood gas analysis...” Now that the attending physician had obtained Ling Ran’s recognition, his self-confidence shot up, and his voice was raised as he barked orders.
Ling Ran played the supporting role obediently with no intention to snatch the attending physician’s authority.

Truth be told, there was no point for a power struggle in the ICU, as there were endless patients to be resuscitated every day and endless orders to be barked every day. No one wanted to make their own life more difficult by getting more work.
However, things were easier now that there were two doctors working together.

With Ling Ran as an assistant, the attending physician easily performed chest drainage. Around 10 ounces of blood-like fluid was drained. When the attending physician saw that the bleeding rate had slowed down, he could not help but breathe a sigh of relief.
Outside the ICU, Zuo Cidian breathed a sigh of relief too. He then turned to smile at Wang Chuanwen and said, “It’s a little boring, isn’t it? This is what hospitals are like.”

“No, I feel more at ease after seeing the way Doctor Ling works.” Wang Chuanwen’s face was full of admiration as he watched Ling Ran who was still performing his tasks meticulously even though he was only an assistant.
There was a proud expression on Zuo Cidian’s face.
